body.title: Record the first repo-scoped base fixtures with an authenticated gh
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations. Follow-up to #68 / PR #111. Tracking: #82.

Depends on: #111 (`cargo xtask record-fixtures` and `parity/fixtures/base/recipe.toml`).

## Why

#111 adds the recorder and the `base` recipe, but nothing has been recorded yet. In the agent sandbox `gh auth status` fails, because `GH_TOKEN` is a placeholder there, so the recorder's guard refuses to run. The guard was deliberately not bypassed. This step needs a real authenticated `gh`: Chris's machine, or an environment where `gh auth status` exits 0.

## Behavior

From a checkout of `rust-main` with #111 merged:

```
gh auth status                                   # must exit 0
cargo xtask record-fixtures --set base
cargo xtask record-fixtures --set base --check   # must report 0 file(s) differ
```

Review the diff of `parity/fixtures/base/repos/gizmo385/gh-lazy/` against the scrub rules in `parity/README.md`, "Recording fixtures". Note that the repo object's `permissions` reflects whoever recorded it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parity/fixtures/base/repos/gizmo385/gh-lazy/` is committed, recorded from the three requests in `parity/fixtures/base/recipe.toml` (repo, raw README, issues page 1).
- [ ] The `#[ignore]` is removed from `crates/fake-gh/tests/recorded_fixtures.rs`, and the test passes: status 200 and a non-empty JSON array for `gh api -i -X GET -F state=all -F page=1 -F per_page=30 /repos/gizmo385/gh-lazy/issues`.
- [ ] `cargo xtask record-fixtures --set base --check` right after recording reports no changes.
- [ ] `cargo test --workspace` passes, including `check-fixtures` and `fake-gh lint` over the new files.
- [ ] Drop "(the first recording is still to be committed ...)" from `parity/README.md`.

## Fixtures

Recorded, not hand-written. They need a real authenticated `gh`.

_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #92 (part of #69).

## What changed

`cargo xtask parity [SCENARIO...]` now runs scenarios against the Python and Rust apps in pseudo-terminals and dumps their screens. It covers everything in #69's shared spec except the structural check (#93) and the diff/HTML output (#94).

- **`xtask/src/parity/`**, with `xtask/src/lib.rs` added so integration tests can drive the runner directly:
  - `cli.rs`: every flag from #69 (`--all`, `--python-only`/`--rust-only`, `--size`, `--out`, `--keep-home`, `--no-build`, `--no-sync`, `--python`, `--retries`, `--jobs`, `--ci`) plus `--validate`. It resolves scenarios, runs `cargo build -p lazy-github -p fake-gh` and `uv sync --frozen --quiet`, runs scenario × size × app with retries and `--jobs` workers, writes `summary.json` and sets exit codes 0/1/2.
  - `scenario.rs`: the v1 format. Serde `Raw*` types use `deny_unknown_fields` and `toml::Spanned`; a validation pass checks one action per step, `checks`/`ignore` only on captures, capture names (unique, `[a-z0-9-]+`), key specs, regexes, `expect` keys naming real captures, sizes, apps, fixture sets, config file and `git_remote`. Every error is `file:line: message`.
  - `keys.rs`: `encode(spec, app_cursor) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KeyError>` for the full table. DECCKM switches arrows and Home/End, and `ctrl+m`/`shift+enter` are rejected.
  - `env.rs`: `prepare()` builds `<run>/{home,bin,work}`. It layers the config (file, then deep-merged overrides, then forced `first_start`/`client_type`), installs fake-gh with `fake_gh::install`, makes the deterministic git repo, and sets the cleared allow-listed env on the `CommandBuilder`. `--keep-home` copies `home/` and `work/` into the report.
  - `runner.rs`: `run(env, steps, out)`. A reader thread feeds `vt100` and `pty.raw`. A CSI state machine answers CPR, DA1, DA2 and DECRQM and leaves `ESC[?u` unanswered; it survives sequences split across reads. Waits poll every 20 ms, `escape` gets a 100 ms pause, and the whole run is bounded by `timeout_ms`. `failure.txt`/`failure.grid.json` are written on timeout or early exit. At the end it kills the app, waits 2 s, and writes `status.json`, with fake-gh misses and errors turned into `fixture_problems`.
  - `grid.rs`: the `Grid` type for `<capture>.grid.json`/`.txt`, which #93 and #94 consume.
  - `summary.rs`: the `summary.json` types and the result rules (pass, fail, rust-not-ready, python-only, rust-only), computed from statuses only until #93.
- `parity/configs/default.json` and `parity/scenarios/startup.toml` (gate false, 160x48 + 100x30, `base`, no git remote, waits for `Repositories` then `capture = "main"`).
- `parity/README.md`: new "The parity harness" section covering running, flags, exit codes, environment, scenario format, how a run works, report layout, dump format, status and results, and testing. It's copied from #69 and is the canonical doc.
- `xtask/src/main.rs`: only the `Parity` subcommand was added.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass locally on Linux.
- Unit tests:
  - scenario parsing: a valid file covering every step kind, defaults, and every invalid shape with its line number, including two keys in a step, an unknown key, `expect` for a missing capture, a duplicate capture and `ctrl+m`
  - every row of the key table, with DECCKM on and off
  - config deep-merge, with the forced fields winning
  - the query responder on a CPR split across two reads, plus every query and the non-queries
  - the grid format: runs, wide characters, JSON shape
  - result rules and CLI flag parsing
- `xtask/tests/runner.rs` (no Python) drives `xtask/tests/bin/echo_tui.rs` (a crossterm example) through the runner. It covers `wait.text`, `wait.regex`, `wait.stable_ms`, `keys`, `type`, `resize`, captures, a forced step timeout with `failure.txt`, the whole-run timeout, an early exit with its code, and a spawn error. The test TUI also checks that the CPR reply has the right position and that crossterm's kitty-keyboard check returns quickly on the DA1 reply. 15 back-to-back runs passed.
- `xtask/tests/python_app.rs` is `#[ignore]` because it needs uv; #70 wires it up. It covers `startup --python-only` at both sizes and the fixture-miss case: a temp copy of `base` without `/user/repos`, passed through a hidden `--fixtures-dir` flag, makes the run exit 1, with `GET /user/repos` and its query in `status.json` `misses`. Both pass locally.
- Manual runs:
  - `cargo xtask parity startup --python-only` exits 0 and writes `main.txt` and `main.grid.json` at both sizes. `fake-gh.log` has `auth status` plus the `/user/repos` request, with no misses.
  - `cargo xtask parity startup` exits 0. The Rust side is `exited with code 0 at step 0`, so the result is `rust-not-ready`.
  - Also tried by hand: `--validate` (an invalid file gives `file:3: ...` and exit 2), `--keep-home`, `--size`, `--jobs 2`, and a `git_remote` scenario (repo, remote and commit created).

body.title: Add cargo xtask record-fixtures and check-fixtures
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Part of #68. The first real recording is follow-up #113.

> **A real recording run is still needed (Chris, or an environment with an authenticated `gh`), tracked in #113.** The recorder, the recipe and all the tests are here. But in this sandbox `gh auth status` fails, so the recorder's own guard refuses to run. `GH_TOKEN` is a placeholder that the egress proxy swaps for a real token, which is why `gh api` itself works here. I did not bypass the guard. #113 covers running `cargo xtask record-fixtures --set base`, committing `parity/fixtures/base/repos/gizmo385/gh-lazy/`, and removing the `#[ignore]` on `crates/fake-gh/tests/recorded_fixtures.rs`.

## What changed

- **`cargo xtask record-fixtures --set <name> [--recipe] [--from-log]... [--gh] [--check] [--dry-run]`** (`xtask/src/fixtures/`):
  - `recipe.rs`: the recipe format, the scope rules and reading fake-gh miss logs.
    - Allowed: `allowed_repos`, `allowed_users` (`/users/<login>[/repos]`), `/emojis` and `/rate_limit`. Only GET.
    - `/user*`, `/notifications*` and `/orgs/*` are refused with a pointer to the hand-written `base` fixtures.
    - Admin-only repo sub-paths are refused even under an allowed repo: `hooks`, `keys`, `invitations`, `collaborators`, `traffic`, `actions/secrets`, `actions/variables`, and `environments/*/secrets` and `environments/*/variables`.
    - Relative path segments are refused.
  - `record.rs`: the network seam is the `Gh` trait. `GhCli` runs `gh api -i -X GET -H "Accept: …" "<path>?<canonical query>"`, 4 at a time (`std::thread::scope`).
    - Guards: not fake-gh, `gh auth status` exits 0, and every file in the set loads.
    - It plans every file before writing anything, so any failure or scrub abort leaves the set untouched.
    - Canonical names come from `fake_gh::fixture`. JSON is pretty-printed with key order preserved. Text over 64 KiB and binary bodies go to `body_file` siblings.
    - Same-key hand-written fixtures are renamed to the canonical name. Fixtures with a `when` or `body` matcher are left alone.
    - `--from-log`: GET misses are appended to the recipe as text, so its comments survive, sorted and de-duplicated. Non-GET misses are listed as write-by-hand. Out-of-scope misses are listed as refused and not appended.
    - After writing, it runs the scrub check and `fake-gh lint` on the set and prints `recorded N, refused M, write-by-hand K`.
  - `scrub.rs`: `scrub(RawResponse, &RecipeEntry) -> Result<ScrubbedResponse, ScrubAbort>` is pure. `Rules::check_fixture` runs the same rules read-only.
    - Headers: only the allow-list is kept.
    - JSON: email, avatar and gravatar values get placeholders. `private: true` and secret patterns abort.
    - Non-UTF-8 bodies abort unless the entry is `binary`.
    - Text emails are replaced, except at `example.com` and `users.noreply.github.com`, `git@<host>` SSH remotes, and image names like `logo@2x.png`.
    - Aborts name the request and the JSON pointer or byte offset.
  - `check.rs`: **`cargo xtask check-fixtures [dir]`** runs over every set under `parity/fixtures/`, hand-written ones included. It's also a `#[test]`, so `cargo test --workspace` enforces it.
- `parity/fixtures/base/recipe.toml`: `GET /repos/gizmo385/gh-lazy`, `/readme` (raw), and `/issues` with `{state: all, page: 1, per_page: 30}`.
- `parity/README.md`: a new "Recording fixtures" section covering the workflow, the recipe, the scope rules, the scrub rules, what gets written, check-fixtures, and a note that `permissions` depends on who records.
- `xtask/src/main.rs`: only adds the two subcommands. `main` now returns `ExitCode` so the tasks can exit 1. That will be a small merge point with #92.

Choices the spec left open:
- `--check` compares in memory instead of in a temp dir. It compares the exact bytes a write would produce, with the committed `note` (the date) kept. It exits 1 when any file differs.
- A recipe entry outside the scope stops the whole run before any request. Refused `--from-log` misses don't stop the run and aren't added to the recipe; they're reported instead.
- Body sibling names are `<name>.body.<ext>`: `diff`, `patch` or `txt` for long text, `bin` for binary.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass. xtask has 39 unit tests.
- Recording and scrubbing run against canned `gh -i` output (`StubGh`). The guard and replay tests run against fake-gh itself, in-process through `fake_gh::app::run`.
  - Scrub:
    - A token in a JSON body and in a text body aborts. A token in a header is dropped by the allow-list.
    - Emails in JSON and in a diff are replaced. SSH remotes and retina image names are kept.
    - `private: true` aborts. Volatile headers are dropped and `Link` is kept.
    - A non-UTF-8 body without `binary` aborts. The other secret patterns are covered too.
    - Secret-shaped strings are built at runtime.
  - Guards:
    - fake-gh is refused, both as a stub version string and as the real in-process fake-gh. A logged-out gh is refused.
    - `/user/repos`, `/notifications`, a repo outside `allowed_repos`, a PUT entry and admin-only sub-paths are refused before any request is sent.
    - A set with a fixture that doesn't load is refused.
  - `--from-log`: a synthetic log with 2 GET misses (one already in the recipe), 1 PUT miss and 1 served line adds exactly 1 entry and reports the PUT, with its body, as write-by-hand. Re-running adds nothing.
  - check-fixtures passes on the committed fixtures. It fails on a temp fixture with a `gmail` address built at runtime, both in a JSON `email` and in a `body_file`.
  - Determinism: `--check` right after recording reports every file unchanged, including `body_file` siblings and a different date. A changed upstream response, reordered keys, compact JSON, a missing trailing newline and a different indent are each reported as changed.
  - Replay: fixtures recorded from canned output are served by fake-gh for the Python argv `api -i -X GET -F state=all -F page=1 -F per_page=30 /repos/o/r/issues` (200, non-empty array), and for the raw README.
  - Replay of the committed recording: `crates/fake-gh/tests/recorded_fixtures.rs` uses the `assert_cmd` test against the copied fake-gh from the spec. It's `#[ignore]` until #113.
- `cargo xtask record-fixtures --set base --dry-run` prints the 3 planned requests. A real run here stops at the `gh auth status` guard, as intended.

## Acceptance criteria (#68)

- [ ] Recipe committed (done). Recording and committing the files moved to #113.
- [ ] fake-gh replays the recorded files: the test is written but `#[ignore]` until #113. The format round-trip is covered now by the in-process replay test.
- [x] Scrub unit tests
- [x] Guard tests
- [x] `--from-log` test
- [x] check-fixtures passes on committed fixtures and fails on a `gmail` fixture
- [x] `--check` after recording reports no changes, now compared byte for byte
- [x] `parity/README.md` "Recording fixtures" section

## Dependencies

- `toml = "1"` (new to the workspace) parses recipes. The spec calls for it.
- `regex = "1"` (new to the workspace) holds the secret and email patterns. The spec calls for it.
- xtask now also uses existing workspace crates: `fake-gh` (path; the fixture types, naming, store scan and lint, so the format is defined in one place), `serde`, `serde_json` (`preserve_order`), `thiserror`, and `form_urlencoded` (the canonical query string).
- `assert_cmd` (already in the workspace) is a new dev-dependency of `fake-gh`, for the replay test the spec asks for.

body.title: Add the Github trait with auth check, current user and repository list
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #89

## What changed

- **`lazy_github_core::github`** (`src/github.rs`)
  - The `Github` trait (`Clone + Send + Sync + 'static`). It uses native return-position `impl Future + Send`, so there's no `async_trait`. It has three methods: `check_auth`, `current_user` and `list_repositories(RepoListQuery)`.
  - `RepoListQuery { kind: RepoKind, sort: RepoSort, direction: SortDirection }`. `RepoListQuery::all()` (equal to `Default`) gives All / FullName / Asc.
  - `CacheTtls` (`From<&CacheSettings>`) and `GhCliOptions { program, hostname, ttls }` (`Default`, `From<&Config>`).
  - `hostname_for_base_url` gives `None` for github.com and api.github.com. For any other host it returns the host, lowercased, with any port kept.
  - `GhCli`, the real impl. It's an `Arc` holding #88's runner (`gh::GhCli`), the TTLs and a `tokio::sync::OnceCell<User>`. Only a successful `current_user` is memoized, and concurrent first calls share one `gh` run.
- **`github::FakeGithub`** (`src/github/fake.rs`, `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util"))`)
  - `Arc<Mutex<State>>` holding canned results and a `Vec<GithubCall>` log, exposed through `calls()`.
  - Builders: `with_user`, `with_repositories` and `with_auth_error`, as specced. I also added `with_user_error` and `with_repositories_error` so #72 can test error toasts.
  - Canned errors repeat on every call. `GhError` isn't `Clone`, so a private `duplicate` rebuilds the `Decode` and `Io` sources from their message and kind.
  - With nothing canned, `check_auth` returns Ok, `list_repositories` returns an empty list, and `current_user` returns `GhError::Command`. It doesn't panic, so a test that forgot `with_user` doesn't vanish inside a spawned task.
- **`lazy_github_core::models`**: `User` (equality and hashing by `id`), `Repository` and `RepositoryPermission`. Unknown fields are ignored and optional fields are `Option` with `#[serde(default)]`. Serializing writes `None` as `null`, which is pydantic's `model_dump` shape.
- **`gh::GhCli` (#88), additive only.** `hostname()` is now `pub`. The `auth status` argv moved into a `pub(crate) auth_status_argv()` so tests can assert it. Behavior is unchanged.
- **Feature** `test-util = []` on `lazy-github-core`.

## Design decisions for review

1. **Two types named `GhCli`.** The spec has the `Github` impl named `GhCli` wrapping #88's runner, and #88's runner is also called `GhCli`. I kept both names: `github::GhCli` composes `gh::GhCli`, and `runner()` exposes the inner one. The alternatives were to rename #88's type (`GhRunner`), which breaks its public API, or to put the `OnceCell<User>` and TTLs inside `gh::GhCli`, which makes the low-level runner depend on models. If you'd rather rename the runner, it's a small follow-up.
2. **`list_repositories` sends `page=1` explicitly (spec deviation).** The spec's argv is `/user/repos?type=all&direction=asc&sort=full_name&per_page=50`. Mine is `…&sort=full_name&page=1&per_page=50`, in Python's parameter order. fake-gh as merged (#104) compares queries exactly and doesn't default a missing `page` to `1`, which #65's notes asked for. Without `page=1`, the Rust request would miss the shared `base` fixture that Python uses. Real gh follows the `Link` URLs, so this changes nothing against GitHub. I filed #109 to decide between fixing it in fake-gh and making this the rule.
3. **The integration test lives in `crates/fake-gh/tests/rust_client.rs`**, next to `python_client.rs`, with `lazy-github-core` and `tokio` as dev-deps of fake-gh.
   - Why there: `CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-gh` is only available inside fake-gh's own package.

body.title: fake-gh: treat a missing `page` query param as `page=1` when matching
body.body:
Found while implementing #89.

#65's notes for #67 asked fake-gh to normalize request keys so that a missing `page` counts as `page=1`. The idea was that a Rust `gh api --paginate /user/repos?...&per_page=50` (no `page`) matches the same fixture as Python's explicit `-F page=1`. fake-gh as merged (#104) doesn't do this: `RequestKey` compares the query exactly, and `parity/README.md` doesn't list it among the key normalization rules.

To get around it, #89's `GhCli::list_repositories` sends `page=1` explicitly (`/user/repos?type=all&direction=asc&sort=full_name&page=1&per_page=50`), so both apps hit `base/user/repos/GET.direction-asc_page-1_per_page-50_sort-full_name_type-all.json`. Real gh follows `Link: rel="next"` URLs, so an explicit first page changes nothing against GitHub.

To decide:
- Add the `page` default to fake-gh's normalization (and the recorder's, #68), so later `--paginate` endpoints don't each need an explicit `page=1`.
- Or make "always send `page=1`" a written rule for `--paginate` calls in PLAN §5 / #89's "How the trait grows", and drop the item from #65's notes.

body.title: Help panel: ? toggles the keybindings side panel
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). This is sub-issue 2 of 2 of #76, which holds the shared `active_bindings` design.

Depends on: #107 (footer, `active_bindings`), #73 (keymap display rules), #74 (main layout), #75 (maximize hides the panel). Stacking on open PRs is fine.

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/ui/app.py` [`action_open_help`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L125-L131): if `HelpPanel` is mounted, remove it; otherwise mount it. That's the Python issue #50 fix.
- [`App.BINDINGS`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L60-L65): `?` is `app.open_help`, "Keybindings", tooltip "Toggle this window".
- `lazy_github/lib/bindings.py`: descriptions and tooltips per id (#73's table).
- Textual 8.2.5 `HelpPanel` and `KeyPanel` (`textual/widgets/_help_panel.py`, `_key_panel.py`): they render `screen.active_bindings` grouped by chain node, including `show=False` bindings.

Python, measured at 160×48 with the repos table focused (`?` pressed once). The panel is the right 52 columns (`floor(0.33 × 160)`), the main area keeps 108, and the footer stops at column 108.

```
▏
▏    ↑ k Cursor up
▏    ↓ j Cursor down
▏      ← Cursor left
▏      → Cursor right
▏   home Home
▏    end End
▏ pgup K Page up
▏ pgdn J Page down
▏ ^pgup ^ Page Left
▏ ^pgdn $ Page Right
▏⏎ space Select table entry
▏^home g Top
▏ ^end G Bottom
▏      l Table scroll right
▏      h Table scroll left
▏
▏      / Search Search in the table
▏
▏     ^f Toggle Favorite …
```

Groups, in order, for that focus (keys merged per action, tooltips after the description):

1. Table: `↑ k Cursor up`, `↓ j Cursor down`, `← Cursor left`, `→ Cursor right`, `home Home`, `end End`, `pgup K Page up`, `pgdn J Page down`, `^pgup ^ Page Left`, `^pgdn $ Page Right`, `⏎ space Select table entry`, `^home g Top`, `^end G Bottom`, `l Table scroll right`, `h Table scroll left`.
2. Searchable table: `/ Search Search in the table`.
3. Section container: `^f Toggle Favorite …`, `O Lookup Repository …`, `u View User …`.
4. Selections pane: `I New Issue …`, `P New PR …`.
5. Main screen: the focus keys `1`–`6` with their tooltips.
6. Screen: `tab Focus Next`, `shift+tab Focus Previous`, `^c super+c Copy selected text`, `^n Notifications …`, `^v Paste link`, `f Follow link …`, `F Follow link (browser) …`.
7. App: `^q q Quit Quit the app and return to the command prompt.`, `^p Command Pallete`, `M Maximize …`, `? Keybindings Toggle this window`.

With details tabs focused, group 1 is `← Previous tab`, `→ Next tab`. With details content focused, it's the scroll bindings (`↑ Scroll Up` … `^pgdn Page Right`). Groups 2–4 only appear for targets inside those containers.

## Behavior

- **Toggle.** `app.open_help` (`?` by default, or its override from #73) opens the panel if it's closed and closes it if it's open. Nothing else closes it.
  - **`escape` does not close the panel.** The original request says it should, but Python doesn't do that. Following the parity rule, Rust matches Python: escape keeps its usual meaning (minimize when maximized, otherwise nothing at the main screen). Note this in PARITY.md as "matches Python; the request's escape-closes wording was wrong". If the maintainer wants escape to close it, that's a small follow-up.
  - Opening it doesn't move focus. The panel isn't focusable and isn't in the tab ring.
- **Placement.** A right-docked column over the full screen height, footer row included. The footer and the main screen take the width to its left.
  - Width `clamp(floor(0.33 × W), 30, 60)`: 52 at 160 columns, 33 at 100.
  - Column 0 of the panel is a left border `▏` in `$primary` on `$panel` background, every row.
  - One blank row at the top, then content with 1 column of padding on the right. Content overflowing the height is cut off; there's no scrolling in M1. Python scrolls with the mouse wheel; that's a known minor diff to record, not to build.
- **Content.** `active_bindings` (#76) for the top screen's chain, re-computed every frame, so it follows focus and keymap overrides.
  - Every group with a non-empty description is listed, including `show = false` ones. Groups with `Hidden` state are skipped (B7: `^n` disappears while notifications are disabled; Python always lists it).
  - Groups from different chain links are separated by one blank line. Within a link, groups keep declaration order.
  - A row is: the keys joined by a space, right-aligned in a column of width `max key text width + 1` across the whole panel, then a space, then the description in `$text`, then a space and the tooltip in `$text-muted`.
  - Keys are drawn in `$footer-key-foreground`, bold. Each key's text is `keymap.key_displays(id)` (#73), so `^q q` and `⏎ space`.
  - Lines too long wrap at word boundaries with a hanging indent to the description column.
  - B14 applies: `^p Command Palette`.
- **Maximize.** While a widget is maximized (#75) the panel isn't drawn and takes no width. It reappears on minimize if it was open. `?` still toggles the stored flag while maximized.
- **Modals.** The panel belongs to the main screen. On the auth screen `?` isn't bound and nothing happens.
- **Mouse.** Clicks on the panel do nothing. Clicks to its left are routed by the `HitMap` as usual.
- **State.** `App { help_open: bool }`. Not persisted.

## Out of scope

- Scrolling the panel: not in M1.
- The command palette (`^p`): its own later issue (PLAN M4); here it's only listed.
- Help for future screens and modals: each one's issue checks its own chain.

## Design notes

- `crates/lazy-github-tui/src/components/help_panel.rs`, a stateless widget:

  ```rust
  pub struct HelpPanel<'a> { pub groups: &'a [ActiveGroup], pub theme: &'a Theme }
  impl Widget for HelpPanel<'_> { fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer); }
  pub fn help_lines(groups: &[ActiveGroup], width: u16) -> Vec<Line<'static>>; // wrapping and alignment, unit-tested
  pub fn help_width(screen_width: u16) -> u16; // clamp(floor(0.33 W), 30, 60)
  ```

- `active_bindings` needs to tell the panel where chain links change. `ActiveGroup.owner` is enough: start a new block whenever `owner` differs from the previous group's.
- `App::render`: if `help_open && !maximized`, split the frame horizontally `[Min(0), Length(help_width(W))]` before #74's `layout()` runs on the left part. #74's `layout` takes the left `Rect`, so the main screen proportions are computed from the narrower width (108 at 160).
- `app.open_help` is handled in `App::update` as `Action::ToggleHelp`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests:
  - [ ] `help_width`: 160 → 52, 100 → 33, 80 → 30, 200 → 60.
  - [ ] `help_lines` for the repos-table chain reproduces the Python group list above, in order, with merged keys and right alignment. Apply B14 and B7.
  - [ ] Wrapping with a hanging indent, at a narrow width.
  - [ ] A `Hidden` group is absent, and a `show = false` group is present.
- [ ] `TestApp` tests:
  - [ ] `?` opens, `?` again closes.
  - [ ] `escape` leaves it open.
  - [ ] Focus change (`2`) re-renders the groups for the PRs table.
  - [ ] With `app.open_help = "f1"` override, `f1` toggles and the panel shows `f1 Keybindings`.
  - [ ] `M` hides the panel; `escape` brings it back.
- [ ] `insta` snapshots: `help_panel_repos_160x48`, `help_panel_details_100x30`, and the styled `help_panel_styles` (`Buffer` debug of a few rows: border, key, description, tooltip styles).
- [ ] Parity scenario `parity/scenarios/help-panel.toml` (`gate = true`), sizes `[[160, 48], [100, 30]]`:
  - Steps: capture `start`, press `?` and capture `open`, press `5` and capture `details`, press `escape` and capture `escape_kept`, press `?` and capture `closed`.
  - Checks `["titles", "focus"]` everywhere. The `open`/`details`/`escape_kept` captures also check the panel text with `expect.<capture>.text_contains`, using lines that B7 and B14 don't touch (for example `"⏎ space Select table entry"`, `"/ Search Search in the table"`, `"? Keybindings Toggle this window"`). Box titles inside the narrower main area must match Python, which proves the width split.
  - Comment pointing at B7 and B14 for why whole-panel text isn't compared.
- [ ] PR note for the parity reviewer: record in PARITY.md that escape doesn't close help (matches Python), and that panel scrolling is a deferred minor diff.

## Fixtures

`parity/fixtures/base`. No recordings.

body.title: Footer: bindings for the focused context
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). This is sub-issue 1 of 2 of #76, which holds the shared `active_bindings` design.

Depends on: #73 (keymap, display rules, `effective_keys`), #74 (footer row, the main screen's chains via #75's `binding_chain`). Stacking on open PRs is fine.

## Python reference

- [`LazyGithubFooter`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L28-L30) and Textual 8.2.5 `Footer`/`FooterKey`. See #76.
- The bindings each widget declares, which is the chain the footer walks:
  - [`_VimLikeDataTable`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L33-L50) and [`SearchableDataTable`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L62-L63)
  - [`ReposContainer`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/repositories.py#L28-L33), [`PullRequestsContainer`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/pull_requests.py#L83-L87), [`IssuesContainer`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/issues.py#L31-L35), [`WorkflowsContainer`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/workflows.py#L97-L98)
  - [`SelectionsPane`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L150), [`MainViewPane`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L279-L286), [`LazyGithubMainScreen`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L444-L449), [`LazyGithub`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L60-L65)

Python footers, captured at 260 columns so nothing is cut off. At narrower widths the same text is clipped at the right edge.

| focus | footer row |
| --- | --- |
| repos table | ` / Search  ^f Toggle Favorite  O Lookup Repository  u View User  I New Issue  P New PR  ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| PRs table | ` / Search  O Lookup Pull Request  E Edit PR  u View User  I New Issue  P New PR  ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| issues table | ` / Search  O Lookup Issue  E Edit Issue  u View User  I New Issue  P New PR  ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| workflows table | ` / Search  T Trigger Workflow  I New Issue  P New PR  ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| details tabs / content | ` ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| repos, `notifications.enabled` | ` / Search  ^f Toggle Favorite  O Lookup Repository  u View User  I New Issue  P New PR  ^n Notifications  ^v Paste link  …` |
| command log, notifications on | ` ^n Notifications  ^v Paste link  f Follow link  F Follow link (browser)  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  M Maximize  ? Keybindings` |
| repos, overrides from #73 | ` ? Search  ^f Toggle Favorite  …  q Quit  ^p Command Pallete  bogus Maximize`. `app.open_help = "h"` is gone because the table's `h` takes it first. |
| auth screen (#106) | ` q Quit` |

At 160×48 the repos footer ends `…  q Quit  ^p Comman`. At 100×30 it ends `…  P New PR  ^v Paste lin`.

## Behavior

- **Placement.** The footer is the last row of the main screen, full width; with the help panel open (#108), it spans the width left of the panel. The background is `$footer-background` across the whole row. It's hidden while a widget is maximized (#75). On the auth screen it's the last row inside the border.
- **Content.** Built from `active_bindings` (#76):
  - Groups with `show`, in order.
  - Each group is drawn as `" {key} "` in the key style (`$footer-key-foreground`, bold, on `$footer-key-background`), followed by `"{description} "` in the description style (`$footer-description-foreground`).
  - Items are concatenated with no other separator, so two spaces appear between items.
  - `{key}` is `keymap.first_key_display(id)` (#73): `^p`, `?`, `/`, `O`, `bogus`.
  - Text past the right edge is clipped, with no ellipsis.
  - Disabled groups are drawn dimmed. None exist in M1.
- **Context.** The footer follows focus immediately. The expected rows are the Python table above, with two intentional diffs:
  - B14: `^p Command Palette` (spelled correctly).
  - B7: `^n Notifications` is shown only while `notifications.enabled`. That matches Python at startup, but Rust also re-checks after Settings saves (M4).
- **Bindings for later features are listed.** `^f`, `O`, `u`, `E`, `I`, `P`, `T`, `^v`, `f`, `F` and `^p` are listed exactly as Python lists them, even though their features land in M2–M4. Pressing them does nothing yet (`Action::Unimplemented`, #75). This keeps the footer cross-check meaningful from M1 on.
- **Modals.** The chain stops at the modal (#72), so App bindings aren't listed: the auth screen shows only `q Quit`.
- **Mouse.**
  - Clicking an item runs its binding as if its key had been pressed: `route_binding(owner, id)`. That's Textual's `FooterKey` click.
  - Hovering highlights nothing. Textual's hover style is optional and not required.

## Out of scope

- The help panel: #108.
- Textual's grouped footer items (`Binding.Group`): LazyGithub defines none.
- Compact footer mode: unused.

## Design notes

- `crates/lazy-github-tui/src/components/footer.rs`, a stateless widget:

  ```rust
  pub struct Footer<'a> { pub groups: &'a [ActiveGroup], pub theme: &'a Theme }
  impl Widget for Footer<'_> { fn render(self, area: Rect, buf: &mut Buffer); }
  pub fn footer_items(groups: &[ActiveGroup]) -> Vec<(String /*key*/, String /*description*/)>; // for tests and the HitMap
  ```

- `App::render` computes `active_bindings` once per frame for the top screen's chain and passes it to `Footer`. #108 passes the same groups to the help panel.
- Each item's `Rect` is registered in the `HitMap` (#105) with `(Owner, BindingId)` for click dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `active_bindings` unit tests:
  - [ ] First key wins across the chain (inner before outer).
  - [ ] A binding whose keys are all taken disappears.
  - [ ] Same-action bindings merge within an owner.
  - [ ] `Hidden` is skipped.
  - [ ] The #73 override example drops `h Keybindings`.
- [ ] `footer_items` tests reproduce every row of the Python table above. For each focus target, compare the joined string; apply B14 by expecting `Command Palette`. Include the notifications-enabled and overrides rows.
- [ ] `insta` text snapshots:
  - [ ] `footer_repos_160x48` and `footer_details_100x30`, to check clipping.
  - [ ] Styled snapshot `footer_styles` (`Buffer` debug), one item, showing key and description styles and the row background.
- [ ] A click on the `M Maximize` footer item maximizes, the same as pressing `M` (`TestApp::click`).
- [ ] Parity scenarios (`gate = true`, cross checks `["titles", "focus", "footer"]`):
  - [ ] `parity/scenarios/footer.toml`, sizes `[[160, 48], [100, 30]]`:
    - Captures at start, then after `2`, `3`, `4` and `5`.
    - `expect.start.footer = ["/ Search", "^f Toggle Favorite", "O Lookup Repository", "u View User", "I New Issue", "P New PR", "^v Paste link", "f Follow link", "F Follow link (browser)", "q Quit"]`. The rest is clipped at 160; check #93's handling of a clipped last item, and trim the list if it treats the clipped item as a mismatch.
    - At 160×48 the `5` capture shows the `^p` item in full. That's B14's intentional diff, so use `checks = ["titles", "focus"]` for that capture, with a comment pointing at B14. Use `expect.<capture>.footer` lists without the `^p` item for the other entries.
  - [ ] `parity/scenarios/footer-notifications.toml`, size `[[260, 40]]`:
    - `notifications.enabled = true`. The status bar is #81's business; ignore it with `ignore = { boxes = [""] }` if needed.
    - `expect.start.footer` includes `^n Notifications` right after `P New PR`.
  - [ ] Flip `keymap-overrides.toml` (#73) to `gate = true`.
- [ ] PR note for the parity reviewer: set the PARITY.md footer row's TERM note to "decided: Textual notation (`^p`)". Also mark B14 and B7 as intentional diffs for the footer.

## Fixtures

`parity/fixtures/base`. With `notifications.enabled`, Python and Rust both fetch notifications, so that scenario also needs #81's notifications fixture (`GET /notifications` empty) in `base`. Hand-written is fine. No recordings.

body.title: Startup flow: gh auth check, auth cache and the GitHub Authentication screen
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). This is sub-issue 2 of 2 of #72, which holds the shared design. It covers the startup flow and the "GitHub Authentication" screen.

Depends on: #105 (runtime), #89 (`check_auth`), #64 (`cache.auth_*`, `core.first_start`), #73 (`app.quit` on this screen), #74 (the info text view it reuses). Stacking on open PRs is fine.

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/ui/app.py`:
  - [`on_ready`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L99-L103): `first_start` shows the backend picker. This is an intentional diff: Rust is gh only (#65, PARITY.md).
  - [`authenticate_with_github`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L70-L90):
    - The check is skipped while `(now - cache.auth_last_checked).total_seconds() < cache.auth_cache_duration`, with naive local time.
    - Otherwise `assert_is_logged_in()` runs, and on success `auth_last_checked = now` is saved and the main screen is pushed.
    - On failure the auth modal is pushed.
- `lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py` [`is_logged_in_to_cli`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py#L105-L116): any failure, including `gh` missing, counts as "not logged in".
- `lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py`:
  - [`GithubCliAuthInstructions`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py#L38-L46): "To proceed, please log into the Github CLI via [green]gh auth login[/green]".
  - [`AuthenticationModal`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py#L49-L74): `border: ascii red`, title "GitHub Authentication", the instructions, a `Rule`, the `LAZY_GITHUB_INFO` markdown and a footer. Its only binding is `app.quit`.
  - [`check_github_cli_access`/`verify_github_cli_access`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py#L113-L124): polls `gh auth status` every 5 s and switches to the main screen on success. It doesn't write `auth_last_checked`.
- `lazy_github/ui/widgets/info.py` [`LAZY_GITHUB_INFO`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/info.py#L7-L32).

Python capture at 100×30 (`gh auth status` exits 1):

```
+- GitHub Authentication --------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|To proceed, please log into the Github CLI via gh auth login                                      |
|                                                                                                  |
|──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────|
|                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                  |
|                           LazyGithub: A Terminal UI For GitHub (0.6.6)                           |
|                                                                                                  |
|  LazyGithub is a terminal UI for interacting with GitHub. You can get started by selecting one   |
|  of the repositories listed in the table on the left. Once you have selected a repository, any   |
   … (info text continues, clipped at the bottom) …
| q Quit                                                                                           |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Behavior

**Startup decision.** The app starts on a blank `Startup` screen; Python also shows nothing until `on_ready`.
- If `cache.auth_last_checked` is set and `local_now - auth_last_checked < auth_cache_duration` seconds (strictly less), the app goes straight to the main screen. No `gh` call is made and nothing is written. A timestamp in the future counts as fresh, as it does in Python.
- Otherwise it issues `GithubRequest::CheckAuth`.
  - **Ok:** set `cache.auth_last_checked = local_now` (naive local, with microseconds as `datetime.now()` has them) and `core.first_start = false`. Save once and show the main screen. Writing `first_start = false` replaces the picker's write (PARITY.md intentional diff).
  - **Any error** (`NotAuthenticated`, `NotInstalled`, `Command`, …): show the auth screen. Log `debug!("Triggering auth with github")` as Python does.

**Auth screen.**
- Full screen, ASCII border (`+`, `-`, `|`) in the theme's error red. #77 decides between literal `red` and a theme slot; Python uses the literal CSS color `red`.
- Border title "GitHub Authentication", drawn as `+- GitHub Authentication ---…+`.
- Row 1 inside the border is the message:
  - `NotAuthenticated` and other errors: "To proceed, please log into the Github CLI via gh auth login". The text `gh auth login` is green.
  - `NotInstalled`: #88's `GhError::NotInstalled` text ("The GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed or not on your PATH. Install it from https://cli.github.com, then run `gh auth login`."). This is an intentional diff: Python treats a missing `gh` as "not logged in".
- A blank row, then a horizontal rule `─` across the inner width, then a blank row.
- Then the `LAZY_GITHUB_INFO` text in #74's `InfoView`, clipped at the bottom.
- The last inner row is the footer, `q Quit` in #76's footer style.
- The chain is modal: only `app.quit` is active. `M`, `?` and `ctrl+p` do nothing here, and the footer shows only `q Quit`. Priority `ctrl+q` still quits.
- Polling: `Effect::StartInterval { id: AuthPoll, every: 5s }` runs `CheckAuth` again on each tick. A new check isn't started while one is in flight.
  - On Ok the app switches to the main screen without writing `auth_last_checked`, as Python doesn't.
  - Logs: `debug!("Github CLI access confirmed")` on success, `debug!("Continuing to wait for Github CLI access...")` on failure.
- `q` quits from the auth screen.

**Main screen entry.** Moving to the main screen cancels `AuthPoll`. The main screen's first focus is set by #74/#75 (the repos table).

## Out of scope

- The device-flow branch (`UserTokenDisplay`) and the backend picker are dropped (PLAN §10 decision 1).
- `--auth-backend` and `AUTH_BACKEND`: M4, CLI row in PARITY.md.
- What the main screen loads on entry (repos, notifications): M2 and #81.

## Design notes

- `screens/startup.rs`: `App::init() -> Vec<Effect>` decides between skipping and checking, using `Clock::local_now()`.
  - Comparison: `local_now.datetime() - auth_last_checked` as a `jiff::Span`, compared in seconds with `auth_cache_duration`.
  - It's a pure function, `fn auth_is_fresh(last: Option<civil::DateTime>, now: civil::DateTime, duration_secs: u64) -> bool`, and is unit tested.
- `screens/auth.rs`:
  - `pub struct AuthScreen { reason: AuthReason /* NotInstalled | NotLoggedIn */, pending: Option<RequestId> }`
  - `pub enum AuthAction { Checked(Result<(), GhError>) }`
  - `bindings() = &[BindingId::AppQuit]`, and the screen is modal for the binding chain.
- The `Github` response for `CheckAuth` is routed by `RequestId` to either the startup decision or `AuthScreen`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `auth_is_fresh` unit tests, with an `auth_cache_duration` of 86400:
  - `None` is not fresh.
  - `now - 86399 s` is fresh.
  - `now - 86400 s` is not fresh.
  - `now + 1 h` is fresh.
- [ ] `TestApp::on_startup()` tests:
  - [ ] Fresh cache: the main screen, no `GithubRequest` and no `SaveConfig`.
  - [ ] Stale cache with `FakeGithub` Ok: one `CheckAuth`, then exactly one `SaveConfig` whose config has `auth_last_checked == FakeClock` local now and `first_start == false`, then the main screen.
  - [ ] `NotAuthenticated`: the auth screen with the login message, and `AuthPoll` started.
  - [ ] Advancing 5 s issues a second `CheckAuth`. Ok switches to main with no `SaveConfig`, and `AuthPoll` is cancelled.
  - [ ] `NotInstalled`: the auth screen with the `NotInstalled` text.
  - [ ] `q` on the auth screen quits. `M` and `?` do nothing there.
- [ ] `insta` snapshots: `auth_not_logged_in_100x30`, `auth_not_logged_in_160x48`, `auth_gh_missing_100x30`.
- [ ] Parity scenarios, sizes `[[160, 48], [100, 30]]`, `gate = true`:
  - [ ] `parity/scenarios/auth-logged-out.toml`:
    - `gh_auth = "logged-out"`, and `config_overrides.cache.auth_last_checked = null`.
    - Wait for the text "GitHub Authentication", then capture `auth`.
    - `expect.auth`: `pane_titles = ["GitHub Authentication"]`, `contains = ["To proceed, please log into the Github CLI via gh auth login"]`, `footer = ["q Quit"]`.
    - Cross checks `["titles", "footer"]`.
  - [ ] `parity/scenarios/auth-cached.toml`:
    - `gh_auth = "logged-out"`, but `config_overrides.cache.auth_last_checked = "2999-01-01T00:00:00"`, so the check is skipped.
    - Capture `main` and expect `contains = ["Repositories"]` and `not_contains = ["GitHub Authentication"]`.
    - Cross check `["titles"]`. This scenario passes once #74 is in.
- [ ] The PR adds the auth-screen row's issue link to PARITY.md, or leaves a note for the parity reviewer.

## Fixtures

`parity/fixtures/base` (#67): `gh auth status` in both states, which the harness selects through `gh_auth`. No new recordings.

body.title: TUI runtime: terminal setup, event loop, Action/Effect types and effect runner
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). This is sub-issue 1 of 2 of #72, which holds the shared design: the `Event`/`Action`/`Effect` types, the `Component` trait, the binding chain, the loop shape and `TestApp`. Read #72 first. This issue builds that design, with a placeholder main screen.

Depends on: #62 (workspace), #64 (`Config`, `ConfigPaths`), #66 (`LogLine`, `LoggingHandle`), #89 (`Github` trait, `FakeGithub`). Implementers can stack on the open PRs for these.

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/cli.py` [`cli`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/cli.py#L15-L24): sets `LAZY_GITHUB_ORIGINAL_PWD` to the cwd if unset, then invokes `run` ([L27-L39](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/cli.py#L27-L39)).
- `lazy_github/ui/app.py` [`LazyGithub.BINDINGS`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L60-L65): `app.quit` is `q`.
- Textual 8.2.5 implicit app keys, measured against the Python app in a PTY:
  - `ctrl+q` quits as a priority binding, so it works even in text inputs.
  - `ctrl+c` doesn't quit. It shows a toast titled "Do you want to quit?" with the message "Press **ctrl+q** to quit the app". The `ctrl+c` text is in bold.
  - Textual restores the terminal on exit and on unhandled exceptions.

## Behavior

- `lazy-github` and `lazy-github run` start the TUI. `--version` keeps working (#62).
- If `LAZY_GITHUB_ORIGINAL_PWD` is unset, it's set to the current directory before anything else runs, as in Python.
- Arguments are parsed before anything else touches the disk (#72's startup order). `--help`, `--version` and usage errors create no config dir and no log file.
- A config that fails to load prints `Error: {#64's message}` to stderr and exits with status 1. The terminal is never touched and there is no fallback to defaults (#72, "Broken config"). This replaces `start_logging`'s fallback-with-`warn!` in `main.rs` from #66.
- Logging is initialized after the config loads and before the terminal is set up; the `LoggingHandle` is dropped after the terminal is restored, so the final log lines are flushed.
- Entering the TUI:
  - alternate screen, raw mode, cursor hidden
  - mouse capture, bracketed paste and focus-change reporting
  - the kitty keyboard protocol flag `DISAMBIGUATE_ESCAPE_CODES`, pushed only when `crossterm::terminal::supports_keyboard_enhancement()` returns `Ok(true)`. This is what makes `shift+enter` and `ctrl+m` distinguishable; see #73.
- Until #74 lands, the screen shows a placeholder main screen: one bordered box titled `LazyGithub` that fills the screen above a blank footer row.
- `q` (`app.quit`, through the keymap from #73, or hard-wired to `q` until #73 merges) and `ctrl+q` exit with status 0. The terminal is restored to exactly its prior state:
  - the kitty flags are popped if they were pushed
  - focus change, bracketed paste and mouse capture are disabled
  - the alternate screen is left, the cursor shown, raw mode turned off
- `ctrl+c` emits `Action::QuitHint`. That raises the toast above through `Action::Notify` (rendered by #79), with severity information, title "Do you want to quit?" and message "Press ctrl+q to quit the app" (the `ctrl+q` is bold). It doesn't quit.
- `SIGTERM` and `SIGHUP` (unix) exit like `q`.
- Panic:
  - The hook restores the terminal first (idempotently, so a later `Drop` is a no-op).
  - It then logs `tracing::error!(panic = %info, "LazyGithub panicked")` to the log file (#66).
  - Last, it calls the previous hook (color-eyre's), which prints the report. Exit status is non-zero.
- Resizing redraws at the new size.
- Command-log lines from #66 are received continuously and kept in a bounded buffer on `App` (the last 1000) for #80 to render. Nothing is shown yet.

## Out of scope

- The startup auth flow and the auth screen: #106. In this issue `App::new` starts directly on the (placeholder) main screen.
- The keymap itself: #73. Real layout: #74. Toast rendering: #79. Until #79 lands, `Action::Notify` records the toast in `App` state and draws nothing.
- Any `Github` request made by the UI. The runner is complete and tested with `FakeGithub`, but no screen issues requests yet.

## Design notes

Follow #72's design notes exactly. They are the contract later issues build on. Specifics for this issue:

**Terminal guard.** It's generic over the writer, so restore is unit-testable without a TTY:

```rust
pub struct TerminalGuard<W: Write> { out: W, kitty_pushed: bool, restored: Arc<AtomicBool> }
impl<W: Write> TerminalGuard<W> {
    pub fn enter(out: W, kitty: bool) -> io::Result<Self>; // writes the enter sequence (raw mode is toggled separately via crossterm::terminal)
    pub fn restore(&mut self) -> io::Result<()>;           // writes the exit sequence once; later calls are no-ops
}
impl<W: Write> Drop for TerminalGuard<W> { fn drop(&mut self) { let _ = self.restore(); } }
pub fn install_panic_hook(restore: impl Fn() + Send + Sync + 'static); // chains the previous hook
```

- Use `ratatui::Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>>` directly. Don't use `ratatui::init()`: it doesn't set the kitty, focus or paste flags, and it installs its own hook.
- `color_eyre::install()` runs in `main` before the hook is installed, so the hook chains to it.

**Runtime.**

```rust
pub struct Runtime<G: Github> { gh: G, tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Event>, paths: ConfigPaths,
                                tasks: HashMap<RequestId, AbortHandle>, timers: HashMap<TimerId, AbortHandle>, saver: ConfigSaver }
impl<G: Github> Runtime<G> {
    pub fn new(gh: G, tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Event>, paths: ConfigPaths) -> Self;
    pub fn execute(&mut self, effect: Effect);          // never blocks; spawns
    pub fn execute_all(&mut self, effects: impl IntoIterator<Item = Effect>);
    pub async fn shutdown(self);                        // abort tasks and timers; await the saver
}
```

- `Effect::Github` spawns `request.run(&gh)` and sends `Event::Github { id, response }`. The `AbortHandle` is stored by id and removed when the task finishes. `Effect::Cancel(id)` aborts it. Aborting drops the future, and `kill_on_drop` (#88) kills the `gh` child.
- `ConfigSaver` is one task fed by a `tokio::sync::watch` channel. `config.save(&paths)` runs in `spawn_blocking`, and each result is sent as `Event::ConfigSaved`. When several saves queue up while one is running, only the newest is written next.
- `App` turns `ConfigSaved(Err(msg))` into `error!("Failed to save config: {msg}")` and an error toast "Failed to save settings: {msg}". Python crashes in this case, so the Rust text is new and is listed as an intentional diff in the PR.
- Timers follow #72: `StartInterval` uses `interval_at(now + every, every)` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay` and is a no-op when that id is running; `StartTimeout` uses `sleep` and replaces a running timer with that id; `CancelTimer` aborts. Each tick sends `Event::Timer(id)`.

**App.**
- `App::new(config, keymap, theme, clock)`.
- `handle_event(&mut self, Event) -> Vec<Effect>` maps an event to zero or more `Action`s and calls `update` for each.
- `update(&mut self, Action) -> Vec<Effect>`.
- `render(&mut self, &mut Frame)`.
- `should_quit()`.
- `next_deadline()`.
- `command_log(&self) -> &VecDeque<LogLine>`.

`Effect::Quit` is returned by `update` and also sets `should_quit`. The loop stops after the current batch.

**`TestApp`** is built here as #72 specifies, with the keys parsed by a minimal stub (single characters, `escape`, `enter`, `tab`, `shift+tab`, `ctrl+<letter>`) until #73 replaces it with the real parser.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo run -p lazy-github` opens the placeholder screen. `q` exits 0 and the shell prompt is intact. Tested manually and recorded in the PR.
- [ ] `TerminalGuard` unit tests over a `Vec<u8>` writer:
  - [ ] `enter(kitty = true)` then `restore` writes the exact expected byte sequences: kitty push/pop, `?1004`, `?2004`, the mouse modes, `?1049`, and cursor hide/show.
  - [ ] `enter(kitty = false)` doesn't write the kitty push or pop.
  - [ ] A second `restore` and the later `Drop` write nothing more.
  - [ ] A panic inside `std::panic::catch_unwind`, with the hook installed and the guard's restore closure, results in the restore sequence being written exactly once.
- [ ] `update` unit tests with `TestApp` and `FakeGithub`:
  - [ ] `q` gives `[Effect::Quit]` and `should_quit()`.
  - [ ] `ctrl+q` gives the same.
  - [ ] `ctrl+c` gives `Action::Notify` with the exact title and message, and doesn't quit.
  - [ ] Key release events are ignored. Build them with `KeyEventKind::Release`.
- [ ] `Runtime` tests on a `current_thread` runtime with `tokio::time::pause()`:
  - [ ] An `Effect::Github { CheckAuth }` against `FakeGithub` delivers `Event::Github` with the same id.
  - [ ] `Cancel` before completion delivers nothing, and `FakeGithub` records the call.
  - [ ] Two `SaveConfig` effects issued while a save is in flight result in exactly two writes: the first and the newest. Test against a temp dir.
  - [ ] `StartInterval` first fires at +`every`, then on schedule; a second `StartInterval` with the same id doesn't add a timer; `CancelTimer` stops it. `StartTimeout` fires once. Use `tokio::time::pause()`.
- [ ] A latest-wins test using a dummy component in `test_util`: start request 1, start request 2 for the same slot, deliver 2 then 1. Only 2's data is applied, and 1 is dropped with a debug log.
- [ ] A `CommandLog` event lands in `App::command_log()`, and the buffer stays capped at 1000.
- [ ] The `main.rs` config-error path is tested with `assert_cmd`: `HOME` points at a temp dir whose `config.json` is `{"issues":{"state_filter":"bogus"}}`. The run exits 1, stderr names `issues.state_filter`, and stdout is empty.
- [ ] `assert_cmd` with `HOME` at an empty temp dir: `--help`, `--version` and `--bogus` (exit 2) leave the temp dir empty. With a broken `config.json`, `--version` still exits 0, and the broken run leaves no `lazy_github.log`.
- [ ] `assert_cmd`: invalid JSON (`{"appearance": `) exits 1 with the line and column in stderr and no traceback-like output.
- [ ] `insta` snapshot `placeholder_main_160x48` from `TestApp::screen(160, 48)`.
- [ ] No parity scenario. The first screens that can be compared with Python arrive in #74 and #106.

## Fixtures

None. Unit tests use `FakeGithub`.

body.title: Build fake-gh and the parity fixture format
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #67

**Stacked on #86** (Cargo workspace, #62). The base is `rust/62-cargo-workspace` for now. I'll retarget it to `rust-main` after #86 merges.

## What changed

`crates/fake-gh` is now a drop-in `gh` for tests and the parity harness. It's a `lib` plus a `[[bin]] fake-gh`; the harness copies the binary to `<tmp>/bin/gh`.

- **Commands:** `gh api` (`-X`, `-H`, `-F`/`-f`, `--input`, `-i`, `--cache`, `--paginate`, `--slurp`, `--hostname`, and `graphql`), `gh auth status`, `gh auth token`, `gh --version`/`gh version` and `gh pr diff -R`. Flags can come before or after the subcommand, so `gh --method PATCH api …` works. Any other flag or command exits 2 and is logged with `error`.
- **Output:** `HTTP/2.0 <status> <reason>\n`, then Go-canonical headers sorted by name, each ending in `\r\n`, then `\r\n` and the body exactly as stored. A default `Content-Type` is added when the fixture has none. On status ≥ 400, gh's error line goes to stderr and the exit code is 1. A miss returns GitHub's 404 body, exits 1 and is logged with `"miss": true`.
- **Request log:** one JSONL line per invocation. The file is held under `File::lock` from the read for `when` through the append.
- **Library modules for #68:**
  - `fixture`: serde types, `Accept::normalize`, `RequestKey::from_url`, `file_name_for`, `dir_for`
  - `store`: `FixtureStore::load` and `lookup`, with `when` > `body` > plain, then earliest set
  - `argv`, `output`, `log`
  - `lint`: `fake-gh lint <set>...`, which runs when argv[0] is `fake-gh`
- **`parity/fixtures/base/`:** hand-written `/user` (`parity-bot`, id 1000001), `/user/repos` with Python's exact page-1 query (3 full-shaped public repos) and `/notifications` (`[]`).
- **`parity/README.md`:** env vars, commands, output, log fields, fixture layout and schema, key normalization, matching and lint.

### Spec points I interpreted

- **Query slug characters.** The spec's example (`per_page-50_sort-full_name`) keeps underscores, but the rule says "outside `[A-Za-z0-9.-]`". I kept `_` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`) so the example holds. A slug over 80 characters becomes `<first 80>-<4-hex FNV-1a of the full query>`.
- **Default method.** It's POST when `--input` is given as well as when fields are, and for `graphql`. That's gh's actual rule. As in gh, fields go to the query string when `--input` supplies the body, and for `graphql` they're nested under `variables`.
- **Which commands need `FAKE_GH_FIXTURES`.** Only `api` and `pr diff` require it (exit 3 when unset). `--version` and `auth` work without it, so #68's guard can detect fake-gh with a bare `gh --version`.
- **`--paginate` logging.** It still writes one log line per invocation. On a miss at page N, the line carries page N's path and query, so `--from-log` (#68) records the right page.
- **Fixture strictness.** Fixture files use `deny_unknown_fields`, so a typo like `"qurey"` is a load error rather than a silently broader matcher.
- **`FAKE_GH_AUTH` values.** Any value other than `logged-in` or `logged-out` exits 3.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass. The fake-gh tests also passed 15 runs in a row (they spawn processes).
- **Unit tests** cover:
  - Argv parsing: every Python shape from the reference table, `-F` vs `-f` typing, the POST default and `--input -`.
  - Key normalization: full URL to path, URL query merged with fields, the accept table, trailing slashes and percent-decoding.
  - Matching precedence: `when` > `body` > plain, an earlier set overriding a later one, a duplicate in one set as a load error, an ambiguous tie at request time.
  - Lint, the log, and output formatting.
- `tests/python_parser.rs` is a Rust port of `_parse_cli_api_response`. It reads fake-gh's `-i` output for a 200 JSON response, a 404 and a text body, and checks the status, the headers (canonical case, sorted) and that the body round-trips. `insta` snapshots record the exact bytes for all three.
- `tests/cli.rs` runs the copied `gh` binary end to end. It covers `--paginate` back to back and with `--slurp`, a missing next page, the miss shape and its log line, exit 2 for unsupported flags, HTTP errors, `body`/`when` with `--input -`, `pr diff` from a `body_file`, auth and version, exit 3 for config errors, overlay precedence, and the `base` fixtures answering Python's argv.
- `tests/concurrency.rs`: 20 parallel invocations give 20 well-formed lines with `seq` 1..20.
- `tests/lint_fixtures.rs` lints every set under `parity/fixtures/` through the library, and also runs the `fake-gh lint` CLI.
- `tests/python_client.rs` is `#[ignore]` (run it with `--ignored`; the #70 job will). It runs the real `run_gh_cli_command(build_command('/user/repos', …))` through `uv run --frozen` and checks `is_success()` and 3 repos. **It passes locally.**
- **Manual check:** I ran `uv sync --frozen`, then `.venv/bin/python -m lazy_github` in tmux at 160x48, with `HOME` set to a temp dir holding `{"core":{"first_start":false},"api":{"client_type":"GITHUB_CLI"}}` and fake-gh first on `PATH`. The Repositories table shows the 3 fixture repos. Here's the top of the screen:

```
┌─ [1] Repositories ───────────────────────────────────────────┐┌─ [5] Details ──────────────
│ ★  Owner       Name         Private                          ││ Introduction
│ ☆  parity-bot  dotfiles     ✘                                ││╸━━━━━━━━━━━━╺━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
│ ☆  parity-bot  hello-world  ✘                                ││
│ ☆  parity-bot  lazy-demo    ✘                                ││
```

  The fake-gh log for that run had two lines: `auth status`, then the `/user/repos` request (`cache_control: max-age=86400`, served from `base/user/repos/GET.direction-asc_page-1_per_page-50_sort-full_name_type-all.json`), with no misses.

## Dependencies

- **`http = "1"`** (new, added to `[workspace.dependencies]`). The spec calls for it: it supplies the canonical reason phrases for the status line. It's small and synchronous, and its only dependencies are `bytes` and `itoa`.
- **`serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`** (already in the workspace). fake-gh turns on `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` feature, as the spec requires. Cargo unifies features across the workspace, so other crates built in the same build also get insertion-ordered maps. That's harmless for deserialization.
- **`insta`** (dev, already in the workspace): byte snapshots.
- I didn't use `assert_cmd`: `std::process::Command` with the copied binary covered every test.

## Notes

- Tests that copy the binary wait out `ETXTBSY` once after copying. Another test thread forking during the copy briefly holds the file open for writing, and exec then fails. `common::install_gh` has the details.
- No Python code was changed.

body.title: Log to a size-rotated file in the Python format, with a command-log stream
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #66

**Stacked on #96 (config) → #86 (workspace).** The base is `rust/64-config`; it will be retargeted to `rust-main` as those merge.

## What changed

New module `crates/lazy-github-core/src/logging/`:

- `rotating.rs`: `RotatingFileWriter` behaves like CPython's `RotatingFileHandler`. It rolls over before a record when the file is non-empty and `len + record >= max_bytes`. Backups shift `.N-1 → .N … .1 → .2`, then the base file moves to `.1`. `max_bytes = 0` never rotates. `backup_count = 0` reopens the same file and keeps appending. A path that isn't a regular file, such as `/dev/null`, a FIFO or a device, never rotates; this is CPython's bpo-45401 guard. It appends across runs and creates missing parent dirs. The file is closed before the renames, and each destination is removed first, so rotation works on Windows. A failed rollover keeps writing rather than losing the record.
- `format.rs`: `LogClock`, `system_clock()`, `LogLine` (its `Display` is the Python line `LEVEL YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS - message key=value`, with `WARN` written as `WARNING`), and the file `FormatEvent`. Fields are rendered the way tracing's default formatter renders them. An error passed as `&dyn Error` gets `name.sources=[…]` in the file only.
- `command_log.rs`: `CommandLogLayer<F>` turns each event into a `LogLine` for a callback sink. `command_log_layer(clock)` returns three things: the layer wrapped in a per-layer `Targets` filter (`lazy_github*` at INFO and above), an `mpsc::Receiver` with capacity 1024, and an `Arc<AtomicU64>` that counts lines dropped by `try_send` when the channel is full.
- `mod.rs`: `LoggingOptions` (with `From<&CoreConfig>`), `LoggingHandle`, and `init`. `LoggingHandle` holds the `WorkerGuard`, the `command_log` receiver and `dropped_command_log_lines()`. `init` wraps the writer in `tracing_appender::non_blocking`. The file filter is `lazy_github=debug` with `warn` as the default, and `LAZY_GITHUB_LOG` overrides it in `Targets` syntax. An unparseable override falls back to the default and is noted with `debug!`, so it stays out of the command log. If the file can't be opened, `init` prints the single stderr line and carries on with only the command log. The module docs hold the info/warn/debug convention.

`crates/lazy-github/src/main.rs` discovers the config paths, loads the config and calls `logging::init`. It then parses arguments with `try_parse`, so `--version` and `--help` run with logging on, and the handle is dropped (which flushes the log) before clap exits. It writes `debug!("Starting LazyGithub <version>")`. #72 should parse arguments first, so that help, version and usage errors have no side effects.

## Notes for review

- **Signature deviation:** the spec has `command_log_layer` returning `(CommandLogLayer<impl Fn(LogLine)>, Receiver<LogLine>)`. It now returns `(impl Layer<S>, Receiver<LogLine>, Arc<AtomicU64>)`. The layer has to be wrapped in `Filtered` because an unfiltered layer makes the subscriber's max level TRACE. The counter belongs to its own channel instead of being a process-wide static.
- **Config load errors in `main`:** this PR falls back to the defaults and records the error with `warn!`. The warning reaches the log file and the command-log buffer, and nothing goes to the terminal. How a broken config should actually be reported belongs to app startup (#72). If `ConfigPaths::discover` fails (no home dir), logging is skipped.
- `logfile_count` is a `u64` in `CoreConfig`, while the spec's `backup_count` is a `u32`. The conversion saturates.
- **tracing-appender terminal output:** the worker drops write errors silently. It can still write to the terminal in two cases, both at shutdown:
  - `eprintln!` if the final flush fails. Flush on this writer can't fail.
  - `WorkerGuard::drop` (0.2.5, `non_blocking.rs:296`) `println!`s to **stdout** if the shutdown message can't be queued within 100 ms, which needs the 128k-line channel to be full at exit. That's unlikely, and by then the TUI will have restored the terminal, but #72 should know about it.

## Dependencies

All of these are already listed in PLAN §4:
- `tracing`, `tracing-appender` (core): the logging stack the spec calls for. `tracing-appender` is used only for `non_blocking`, and it brings in `time`, `crossbeam-channel` and `symlink`.
- `tracing-subscriber` (core, features `fmt`, `registry`, `std`). The workspace entry is now `default-features = false` so that `env-filter`, `tracing-log` and `ansi` stay out, as the spec says.
- `tokio` (core, feature `sync`): the bounded `mpsc` channel for the command log.
- `lazy-github-core`, `tracing` (binary): to call `init` from `main`.
- `assert_cmd` (binary, dev): the stderr test runs the real binary.

## How tested

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass on toolchain 1.97.0.

- Formatter (fixed clock): `info!("Selected repo foo/bar")` renders as `INFO 2026-10-25 01:02:03 - Selected repo foo/bar`, and `warn!` renders with `WARNING`. Also tested: the names of all five levels, fields after the message, fields without a message, `%err`, and an error source chain.
- `RotatingFileWriter` in a temp dir:
  - rotation at `max_bytes = 100`, `backup_count = 2`: only `log`, `log.1` and `log.2` exist, the record order shows `.1` is newer than `.2`, and every file is under the limit
  - `max_bytes = 0`
  - `backup_count = 0`
  - reopening counts the existing size
  - appending across opens
  - an empty file with an oversized first record
  - missing parent dirs
  - Unix only: a symlink in the temp dir pointing to `/dev/null` never rotates. No `.1` appears and the link stays in place; `/dev` is only written to.
- Filter, through the real `non_blocking` file layer:
  - with the default filter, app `debug!` is kept, foreign `info!` is dropped and foreign `warn!` is kept
  - an env override replaces the default
  - an invalid override falls back to the default
  - the file appends after an existing Python line
- Command log (`with_default`): `info!`, `error!` and `warn!` from `lazy_github_*` arrive in order as `LogLine`s, and debug and foreign events don't. Error sources are left out. Pushing 1034 events into the 1024-slot channel keeps the first 1024, counts exactly 10 dropped lines and doesn't block.
- `init`, with each case in its own test binary because the subscriber is process-wide:
  - it creates missing parent dirs, writes the file, and buffers command-log lines before anything reads them
  - with an unopenable path it still returns a working command log
- Binary (`assert_cmd`, `HOME` set to a temp dir; not run on Windows, which finds its config dir without `HOME`):
  - `lazy-github --version` has empty stderr and writes the DEBUG start line to `~/.config/lazy-github/lazy_github.log`
  - with `core.logfile_path` under a regular file, stderr is exactly one `LazyGithub: could not open log file …; continuing without a log file` line and the exit status is success

No parity scenario or snapshot, as the spec says; #80 adds those.

body.title: Searchable table: lazy-loading hook
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). Sub-issue 3 of 3 of #78, which holds the shared model. Read #78 first.

Depends on: #100 (table core). It can be built in parallel with #101.

## Python reference

- [`LazilyLoadedDataTable`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L180-L250):
  - `load_more_data_buffer = 5`
  - `current_batch` starts at 0
  - `can_load_more` starts true
  - `clear_rows` resets both and drops the load function ([L224-L229](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L224-L229))
  - `load_more_data` runs under an `asyncio.Lock` ([L231-L246](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L231-L246))
  - it's triggered on every `RowHighlighted` ([L248-L250](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L248-L250))
- How callers drive it:
  - `ui/widgets/pull_requests.py` [`on_issues_and_pull_requests_fetched`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/pull_requests.py#L179-L187) adds the first page, sets the load function, `can_load_more = True` and `current_batch = 1`.
  - [`fetch_more_pull_requests`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/pull_requests.py#L142-L154) returns `[]` with no repo.
  - Issues and workflows do the same; notifications use batch 50.
- Textual posts `RowHighlighted` when the cursor index changes, and when the first row appears in an empty table ([`add_row`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/widgets/_data_table.py#L1722-L1732)). It does not post it on a sort or a replace that leaves the index unchanged.

## Behavior

A lazy table starts with lazy loading **off**. The owner turns it on with `enable_lazy_load(batch_size, current_batch)` after its first page, the way Python sets the load function.

- **When the check runs.** Whenever the cursor index changes, and when a batch insert turns an empty table non-empty (cursor 0).
- **The check.**
  - Skip it if lazy loading is off or `can_load_more` is false.
  - `remaining = items().len() - cursor`. This counts all loaded items, including any hidden by a search, exactly as Python does with `len(self.items)`.
  - If `remaining <= 5`, ask for page `current_batch + 1` with `per_page = batch_size`.
- **While a page is in flight**, further checks don't start a second request. The highest cursor index seen meanwhile is remembered and re-checked once when the page lands. That matches the effect of Python's lock queue, where each queued highlight re-checks after the fetch.
- **When the page lands.**
  - `current_batch += 1`.
  - An empty page sets `can_load_more = false`.
  - The items are inserted as with `insert_many`: sorted, unfiltered, replacing equal keys.
  - The owner is told the item set changed, so M2 can write the cache, which Python does via `add_items(write_to_cache=True)`.
- **A failed page** leaves `current_batch` and `can_load_more` unchanged and logs `warn!`. The next cursor move retries. Python's behavior here belongs to each fetcher: an uncaught exception in a `@work` worker exits the app. The M2 issues spec the user-visible error per table; this hook only must not lose state.
- **`clear()`** turns lazy loading off, resets `current_batch` to 0 and `can_load_more` to true, and bumps `generation`. A page that arrives with an older generation is dropped, so a late page for repo A never lands in repo B's table.
- **No spinner.** Python shows none for follow-up pages either.

## Out of scope

- The fetchers, page sizes per table, and the first-page wiring: M2 (PRs, issues, workflows) and M4 (notifications).
- Cache writes: M2.

## Design notes

```rust
pub struct LazyLoad { batch_size: u32, current_batch: u32, can_load_more: bool, in_flight: Option<u32 /*page*/>, pending_cursor: Option<usize> }
impl<T: TableItem> SearchableTable<T> {
    pub fn enable_lazy_load(&mut self, batch_size: u32, current_batch: u32);
    pub fn page_loaded(&mut self, generation: u64, page: u32, result: Result<Vec<T>, GhError>, cx: &T::Ctx) -> Option<TableEvent<T::Key>>; // may immediately yield the next LoadMore
}
// TableEvent::LoadMore { generation, page, per_page } comes out of handle_key / insert_many when the check fires.
```

- The check is a pure function `fn should_load(items: usize, cursor: usize, lazy: &LazyLoad) -> Option<u32>` that is easy to unit-test.
- `insert_many` returns `Option<TableEvent>` so the "first row appeared" check can fire from a bulk insert.
- The owner maps `LoadMore` to its own `Effect` (for example `Effect::Github(GithubRequest::ListPullRequests { repo, page, per_page, generation })`). It routes the completion event back to `page_loaded`. The `generation` tag is the stale-response guard #72 asks for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests with a test `TableItem`:
  - no request while disabled
  - with 30 items, moving the cursor to 24 requests page 2 (`remaining = 6` → no; 25 → yes)
  - a 3-item first page requests page 2 as soon as it's inserted
  - an empty page stops further requests
  - an in-flight page suppresses duplicates, and the pending cursor re-check fires once after it lands
  - an error keeps state and the next move retries
  - `clear()` drops a late page by generation
  - a hidden (filtered) item still counts toward `remaining`
- [ ] `insta` snapshot `lazy_after_page_2`: rows from two pages sorted together, number descending.
- [ ] Parity scenario `parity/scenarios/table-lazy-load.toml`, `gate = false` (flipped by the M2 PR-table issue). Fixtures `prs-70`, `git_remote = "parity-bot/lazy-fixture"`. Steps:
  - wait for "Pull Requests"
  - `2`, `G`
  - wait for the fake-gh log to show `page=2`
  - capture `after-page-2`
  - `G`
  - wait for `page=3`
  - capture `after-page-3`

  Checks: `rows`, `cursor`.

## Fixtures

`parity/fixtures/prs-70`: `GET /repos/parity-bot/lazy-fixture/issues` pages 1–3 of `per_page=30` (30, 30, 10 PR items) and page 4 empty, with the query parameters Python sends. The exact parameters come from the M2 PR spec; until then hand-write them from `lib/github/issues.py` `list_issues`. The repo must be in `repos-60`.
