body.title: Searchable table: / search input and filtering
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). Sub-issue 2 of 3 of #78, which holds the shared model. Read #78 first.

Depends on: #100 (table core).

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py`:
  - [`ToggleableSearchInput._on_blur`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L53-L59)
  - [`SearchableDataTable.__init__`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L62-L95) (placeholder `"Search..."`, hidden and unfocusable at start, `margin-bottom: 1`)
  - [`action_focus_search`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L107-L111)
  - [`handle_submitted_search`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L166-L177)
- [`common.table.search`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/bindings.py#L90) (`/`, shown in the footer, tooltip "Search in the table"). It's bound on the container, so it works whenever focus is inside the table component.
- Textual 8.2.5 [`Input`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/widgets/_input.py): `BINDINGS` L76-L130 and `DEFAULT_CSS` L177-L225 (height 3, `border: tall $border-blurred`, `padding: 0 2`, `$surface`; focused `border: tall $border` with a 5% `$foreground` tint; placeholder `$text-disabled`; cursor `$input-cursor-*`).

## Behavior

**Opening.** `common.table.search` (`/`, overridable; Python may save it as `slash`) pressed while the table has focus:
- shows the search box above the table, taking 3 rows plus 1 blank row below it, so the table moves down by 4;
- focuses the box, keeping any text already in it.

The box is a full-width single-line input with Textual's tall border (`▊▔▎` / `▊ ▎` / `▊▁▎`) in `$border` when focused and `$border-blurred` when not. When empty it shows the placeholder `Search...` in `$text-disabled`.

**Typing.** While the box has focus, printable keys (including `q`, `j`, `/`, space) go into the text. Editing keys, from Textual's `Input`:

| Key | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `left` / `right` | Move the cursor one character. |
| `ctrl+left` / `ctrl+right` | Move one word. |
| `home`, `ctrl+a` / `end`, `ctrl+e` | Go to the start / end. |
| `backspace` | Delete the character to the left. |
| `delete`, `ctrl+d` | Delete the character to the right. |
| `ctrl+w` / `ctrl+f` | Delete the word to the left / right. |
| `ctrl+u` / `ctrl+k` | Delete everything to the left / right. |
| bracketed paste | Insert the pasted text; only its first line. |
| `enter` | Submit (below). |

- `tab`/`shift+tab` move focus as usual (#75); `tab` from the box goes to the table.
- `escape` does nothing in the box. It isn't bound there in Python. When a section is maximized, `escape` still restores it (#75).

**Submitting** (`enter` in the box) applies the filter once:
1. `q = text.trim().to_lowercase()`.
2. For each item, in `items()` insertion order: it matches when `q` is empty, or when `q` is a substring of `py_repr(cells).to_lowercase()`.
3. Every item is reinserted in that order, which resets tie order to `items()` order, and the non-matching ones are hidden. Then the cursor goes to row 0 and the scroll to (0, 0), because Textual's `clear` does that.
4. Focus moves to the table.

**The search text is Python's `str()` of the row tuple**, so the match runs across the whole row representation, not per cell. `py_repr` reproduces it exactly:
- A tuple is `(` + the items joined by `", "` + `)`.
- An `Int` is decimal.
- A `Str` is Python's `repr`: single quotes, or double quotes when the text contains `'` and no `"`.
  - Escapes: `\\`, the quote in use, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`.
  - Other non-printable characters become `\xhh`, `\uhhhh` or `\Uhhhhhhhh`. "Non-printable" follows `str.isprintable`: general categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, and Zs other than U+0020.
- A `DateTime` is `datetime.datetime(Y, M, D, h, m[, s[, us]])`: microseconds are dropped when 0, then seconds when 0 too.

Consequences you can see, all as in Python:
- `', 'gh` matches every row whose next cell starts with `gh`.
- `'` or `(` matches every row.
- `green` matches every favorited repo, because the star cell's value is `[green]★[/]`.
- Notification rows (M4) don't match a query like `2026-01` against their date column.

**After submitting.**
- Text left in the box stays visible, and the filter stays applied. Pressing `/` again re-opens the box with that text.
- When the box loses focus and its trimmed text is empty, it hides, giving the table back its 4 rows. Submitting an empty query therefore shows all rows and hides the box.
- Text that was typed but not submitted (e.g. focus moved with `tab`) doesn't filter. The box stays visible because it isn't empty.
- Items inserted after a filter (`insert`, a lazy page, a re-added key) are shown even when they don't match: in Python `add_item` appends to the table unconditionally. A replaced key that was hidden becomes visible.
- `clear()` empties the items and the hidden set. It leaves the box and its text alone; Python's `clear_rows` doesn't touch the input either.

## Out of scope

- Clipboard and selection keys in the box: see #78 Out of scope.
- Fuzzy matching. Python's table search is a plain substring match; `nucleo` is for the command palette and settings search (M4).
- The footer showing "/ Search": #76.

## Design notes

- **`text_input.rs`.** `TextInput { value: String, cursor: usize /* char index */, placeholder: &'static str }`, with `handle_key(key) -> InputOutcome { Changed, Submitted, Ignored }`, `handle_paste(&str)` and `render(frame, area, &Theme, focused)`.
  - Word movement and deletion follow Textual's rules: a word boundary is a change between `\w` and non-`\w`, the same regex Textual's `Input` uses. Port its `_cursor_left_word`/`_cursor_right_word` logic.
  - `tui-textarea` (PLAN §4) is for the multi-line editors. For this single-line box a small owned type is simpler and easier to style exactly. Record that choice here; the M3 modals can reuse `TextInput`.
- **`search.rs`.** `SearchBox { input: TextInput, visible: bool }` on `SearchableTable`, with focus inside the component as an enum `TableFocus { Table, Search }` that #75's focus model can query.
  - The table's `handle_key` sends keys to the box when it is focused, and checks `common.table.search` when the table is focused.
  - On `Submitted` it runs `apply_filter`, a pure function over `(items, cells, query) -> hidden set`.
- **`py_repr.rs`.** `fn py_repr_row(cells: &[CellValue]) -> String` plus `fn py_repr_str(&str) -> String`.
  - Use the `unicode-general-category` crate for `isprintable` (tiny, no deps).
  - Pin it with golden tests generated by Python (below).
- Search matching computes `py_repr_row(..).to_lowercase()` on each submit. It's O(rows) with no caching, which is fine at these sizes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `py_repr` golden tests. A committed script `crates/lazy-github-tui/tests/fixtures/py_repr/generate.py` (run with `uv run python …`) writes `cases.json` with Python's `str(tuple)` for:
  - ints, including negative
  - plain ASCII
  - a `'`, a `"`, both
  - a backslash
  - `\n`/`\t`
  - `\x7f`
  - U+200B
  - an emoji
  - a CJK title
  - `[green]★[/]`
  - naive datetimes with and without seconds and microseconds

  The Rust test asserts byte equality for every case.
- [ ] Filter unit tests:
  - case-insensitive substring
  - trimmed query
  - empty query restores everything
  - the cross-cell match `', 'gh`
  - cursor and scroll reset to 0 after submit
  - tie order reset to `items()` order
  - an insert after a filter shows a non-matching row
  - `clear()` keeps the box text
- [ ] `TextInput` unit tests for every key in the table above, including word movement over `foo-bar baz`, and paste of multi-line text inserting only the first line.
- [ ] `insta` snapshots (40×12, `textual-dark`):
  - `search_open_empty` (placeholder, focused)
  - `search_typed`
  - `search_submitted_filtered` (box blurred with text, table focused, filtered rows)
  - `search_closed_after_empty_submit`
- [ ] Parity scenario `parity/scenarios/table-search.toml`, `gate = false` (flipped by the M2 repos-table issue). Fixtures `repos-60`. Steps:
  - `1`, `/`, capture `open`
  - type `lazy`, `enter`, capture `filtered`
  - `/`, `ctrl+u`, type `', 'gh`, `enter`, capture `cross-cell`
  - `/`, `ctrl+u`, `enter`, capture `cleared`

  Checks: `rows`, `cursor`, `focus`.

## Fixtures

`repos-60` from #100, with at least three repos whose name contains `lazy` and two whose name starts with `gh`.

body.title: Searchable table: rows, sorting, cursor, scrolling and rendering
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). Sub-issue 1 of 3 of #78, which holds the shared model (`TableItem`, `Cell`, `CellValue`, state, `TableEvent`). Read #78 first.

Depends on: #72 (component contract), #73 (keymap), #77 (theme).

## Python reference

- [`_VimLikeDataTable`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L33-L50) and [`common.table.*` bindings](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/bindings.py#L88-L108).
- [`SearchableDataTable.add_item` / `add_items` / `clear_rows` / `sort_table`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L97-L164).
- The `loading = True` overlay, e.g. [`repositories.py` `on_mount`/`load_repos`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/repositories.py#L66-L141).
- Textual 8.2.5:
  - [`DataTable`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/widgets/_data_table.py): `BINDINGS` L273-L285, `DEFAULT_CSS` L327-L400, `action_page_down`/`page_up` L2704-L2750, `action_scroll_top`/`bottom` L2762-L2780, `_on_click` L2669-L2703, `_clamp_cursor_coordinate` L1317-L1322, `sort` L2592-L2632.
  - [`LoadingIndicator`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/widgets/_loading_indicator.py).
  - `Widget.focusable`, which ignores the loading state of ancestors, so the inner table keeps focus and keys while its container shows the spinner.

## Behavior

**Layout and look** (all colors are #77 theme variables):

- **Header.** One row. Each column's header text is bold, in `$foreground` on `$panel`.
- **Rows.** One line each, `$foreground` on `$surface`. No zebra stripes: Python never turns them on.
- **Columns.** Each column is as wide as its widest cell or header, plus one space of padding on each side. Columns are never truncated or stretched. A row narrower than the viewport leaves the rest of the line `$surface`.
- **Height.** The table is `height: auto`: header plus rows, capped at its area. Below the last row the parent's background shows, not `$surface`. That's what makes short tables look short in Python.
- **Scrollbars.**
  - A vertical scrollbar, 2 columns wide, appears at the right edge only when the rows don't fit.
  - A horizontal scrollbar, 1 row, appears at the bottom only when the columns don't fit.
  - Each takes space from the viewport, as in Textual.
  - Colors: `$scrollbar` thumb on `$scrollbar-background`.
- **Cursor row** (always shown, row mode):
  - Table focused: `$block-cursor-background` with `$block-cursor-foreground` and `$block-cursor-text-style` (bold in `textual-dark`).
  - Table not focused: `$block-cursor-blurred-background` composited over `$surface`, `$block-cursor-blurred-foreground`, `$block-cursor-blurred-text-style`.
- **Focused tint.** While focused, the whole table, header included, is tinted with `$foreground` at 5% (Textual `background-tint`).
- **Hover.** With the mouse over a row that isn't the cursor row, that row's background gets `$block-hover-background` composited on top.
- **Empty table.** The header only.

**Keys while the table has focus**, by binding id (defaults from `lib/bindings.py`, overridable through #73), then Textual's fixed keys:

| Binding id | Default | Fixed Textual keys | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `common.table.cursor_down` | `j` | `down` | Cursor +1, clamped to the last row. Scroll so the cursor row is visible. |
| `common.table.cursor_up` | `k` | `up` | Cursor −1, clamped to 0. |
| `common.table.page_down` | `J` | `pagedown` | With `h` = viewport body height (rows minus header and horizontal scrollbar): cursor += `h`, clamped to the last row, and the view scrolls down by `h`. Textual's algorithm: count rows from the cursor until their heights exceed `h`. |
| `common.table.page_up` | `K` | `pageup` | Mirror: cursor −= `h`, clamped to 0, and the view scrolls up by `h`. |
| `common.table.scroll_top` | `g` | `ctrl+home` | Cursor to row 0. |
| `common.table.scroll_bottom` | `G` | `ctrl+end` | Cursor to the last row. |
| `common.table.scroll_right` | `l` | `right` | Horizontal scroll +1 column of text, clamped to the max. Does nothing when the content fits. |
| `common.table.scroll_left` | `h` | `left` | Horizontal scroll −1, clamped to 0. |
| `common.table.page_right` | `$` | `ctrl+pagedown` | Horizontal scroll + viewport width, clamped. |
| `common.table.page_left` | `^` | `ctrl+pageup` | Horizontal scroll − viewport width, clamped. |
| (none) | | `end` / `home` | Horizontal scroll to the max / to 0. |
| `common.table.select` | `enter,space` | `enter` | Emits `Selected(key of the cursor row)`. Does nothing on an empty table. `enter` keeps working even if the id is rebound, because Textual's `DataTable` binding has no id. |

- `H` and `L` do nothing (Py bug B9 recommendation, which is also Python's real behavior).
- Every other key is returned unhandled to the parent.
- All these keys also work while the loading overlay is shown, as in Python.

**Mouse.**
- Clicking a row moves the cursor there. Clicking the cell under the cursor again (same row and same column) emits `Selected`.
- Clicking the header does nothing.
- The wheel scrolls the view by 1 row per notch without moving the cursor. Textual's DataTable scrolls 1 line per wheel event; check this in the parity capture and adjust.

**Inserting and clearing.**
- `insert` appends the row. If the key exists, the old row is removed first: the new row goes to the end of its tie group, and the item keeps its slot in `items()`. All rows are then re-sorted.
- `clear()` removes everything, resets the cursor to 0 and both scroll offsets to 0, and bumps `generation`.
- The cursor stays at the same index through every insert and sort, clamped to `rows.len() - 1`.

**Loading overlay.** `set_loading(true)` hides the whole component area: table, and search box when shown (#101).
- The area is painted `$boost` over `$background`.
- Five dots `● ● ● ● ●` are centered, animated with Textual's gradient (`$background` blended 10% toward `$primary`, then `$primary`, then `$primary` lightened 10%), phase `(t * 0.8 - i/8) mod 1`.
- When the environment has `TEXTUAL_ANIMATIONS=none`, as the parity harness sets for both apps, the overlay shows the static text `Loading...` in `$primary` instead.
- `set_loading(false)` restores the table.

## Out of scope

- The search input and filtering: #101.
- Lazy loading: #102.
- Focus movement into and out of the table (`tab`, `1`–`6`): #75.
- What `Selected` does: M2.

## Design notes

- `model.rs`:
  - `RowEntry { key, cells: Vec<Cell>, seq: u64 }`. A table-wide counter assigns `seq` on each insertion into `rows`.
  - Sorting is `rows.sort_by(|a, b| cmp(a, b))`: compare `cells[col].value` (reversed when `reverse`), then `seq` ascending. A stable `sort_by` on `(value, seq)` gives Python's tie order for both directions.
  - Keep the cursor/scroll arithmetic in pure functions over `(row_count, cursor, scroll_y, viewport_h)` so it can be unit-tested without rendering.
- `render.rs`:
  - Compute column widths with `unicode-width` (ratatui already depends on it).
  - Build a `Line` per visible row, styling each span from `Cell::display` patched with the row style (cursor, hover, base).
  - Draw the header and body with `Paragraph::scroll((0, scroll_x))`, and the scrollbars with ratatui's `Scrollbar` (symbols chosen to look like Textual's).
  - Keep the viewport size from the last render in state (`Cell<Rect>`, or set it in `render` through `&mut self` if #72 allows it), so `page_down` knows `h`.
- Animation: the overlay needs redraws. Read the elapsed time from the #72 tick or event-loop clock; there's no `Effect`. Don't read `Instant::now()` inside `render`. Pass a `now` in, so snapshots are deterministic.
- `TEXTUAL_ANIMATIONS` is read once at startup into an `AppOptions { animations: bool }` that #72 can grow. It's a compatibility switch, not a user setting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests (model, no rendering):
  - stable sort ascending and descending with ties, including a re-inserted key moving to the end of its tie group while keeping its `items()` position
  - cursor clamping after removals, and the cursor staying at its index after inserts and sorts
  - `page_down`/`page_up` targets for `h = 5` at the top, middle and end of 12 rows
  - `scroll_top`/`scroll_bottom`
  - horizontal scroll clamping, including no-op when the content fits
  - `select` on an empty table returns nothing
  - `H`/`L` are unhandled
  - all ids resolved through #73's keymap, plus a test with `common.table.cursor_down` overridden to `n` (now `j` is unhandled and `down` still works)
- [ ] `insta` snapshots (`TestBackend`, buffer dump including styles), with a test `TableItem` of 12 rows × 4 columns (one column with a long title) in a 40×8 area, under `textual-dark`:
  - `table_initial_focused`
  - `table_initial_blurred`
  - `table_after_J` (paged)
  - `table_after_G`
  - `table_scrolled_right` (after `$`)
  - `table_empty`
  - `table_loading_static` (animations off)
  - `table_hover`
- [ ] Parity scenario `parity/scenarios/table-navigation.toml`, `gate = false` (flipped by the M2 repos-table issue). Fixtures `repos-60`, size 160×48. Steps:
  - wait for "Repositories"
  - capture `initial`
  - keys `1`, `j`, `j`, capture `down-2`
  - `J`, capture `page-down`
  - `G`, capture `bottom`
  - `g`, capture `top`
  - `$`, capture `page-right`
  - `^`, capture `page-left`

  Checks: `rows`, `cursor`, `headers`.

## Fixtures

`parity/fixtures/repos-60`: `GET /user/repos?type=all&direction=asc&sort=full_name` as two pages of 50 and 10 (`Link: rel="next"`), 60 repos with names long enough that the table overflows 100 columns at 100×30. Owners `parity-bot` and `parity-org`. Two repos are listed in the scenario config's `repositories.favorites`. Hand-written per #67's format; no recording needed. The format and harness come from #67 and #92.

body.title: Detect terminal color depth and downsample theme colors
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). Sub-issue 2 of 2 of #77, which holds the shared design. Read #77 first.

Depends on: #98 (`Theme`, `ThemeColor`).

## Python reference

Textual hands colors to Rich, and Rich reduces them to what the terminal supports:

- Rich 15.0.0 (`uv.lock`) [`Console._detect_color_system`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/v15.0.0/rich/console.py#L789-L811):
  - `COLORTERM` in `truecolor`/`24bit` → truecolor.
  - Otherwise the part of `TERM` after the last `-` picks the mode: `256color` → 8-bit, `kitty` → 8-bit, `16color` → standard.
  - Anything else → standard (16 colors).
  - Not a terminal, or `TERM` in `dumb`/`unknown` → no color.
- Textual reads `TEXTUAL_COLOR_SYSTEM` (default `auto`) in [`constants.py`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/constants.py#L146).
- [`Color.downgrade`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/v15.0.0/rich/color.py#L513-L553):
  - Truecolor → 8-bit: HLS saturation < 0.15 is grayscale, `gray = round(l * 25)`, giving 16, 231 or 231+gray. Otherwise the 6×6×6 cube: `v/95` when `v < 95`, else `1 + (v - 95)/40`, rounded, `16 + 36r + 6g + b`.
  - → standard: `STANDARD_PALETTE.match(triplet)`, the weighted-distance nearest of Rich's 16 palette colors ([`palette.py`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/v15.0.0/rich/palette.py), [`_palettes.py`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/v15.0.0/rich/_palettes.py)).

## Behavior

- In a truecolor terminal (`COLORTERM=truecolor`, which the parity harness sets), colors are exact RGB.
- With `TERM=xterm-256color` and no `COLORTERM`, every RGB color is shown as the xterm-256 index Rich would choose. So the Python and Rust apps look the same in, for example, macOS Terminal.app.
- With a 16-color `TERM` (e.g. plain `xterm`, `screen`), RGB colors become the nearest of the 16 ANSI colors by Rich's metric.
- `NO_COLOR` set to any value (Textual's [`App.__init__`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/app.py#L600-L603)): RGB colors are shown in gray using Textual's [`Color.monochrome`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/color.py#L385-L394), `gray = round(0.2126r + 0.7152g + 0.0722b)`, before any downsampling. Under an ANSI theme, `NO_COLOR` removes all colors (`Color::Reset`), as Textual's `NoColor` filter does.
- ANSI theme colors pass through unchanged in every depth.

## Out of scope

- Palettes and compositing: #98.
- Windows console detection: Windows is a stretch goal (PLAN §7). Treat Windows as truecolor and label any gap `platform: windows`.

## Design notes

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ColorDepth { TrueColor, EightBit, Standard, None }
impl ColorDepth {
    pub fn detect(env: &impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Self; // Rich's rules, plus TEXTUAL_COLOR_SYSTEM=truecolor|256|standard|auto for parity debugging
}
pub struct ColorMode { pub depth: ColorDepth, pub no_color: bool }
impl ColorMode { pub fn detect(env: &impl Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Self; }
pub fn downsample(rgb: Rgb, mode: ColorMode) -> ratatui::style::Color; // monochrome if no_color, then Rgb / Indexed(n) / named ANSI / Reset
```

- `depth.rs` in `crates/lazy-github-tui/src/theme/`. `ColorMode::detect` runs once in the binary before the terminal is set up, reading the process env. The value is stored in `Theme` and applied by `Theme::color` after compositing, so components never see it.
- The env reader is injected so the function is unit-testable without touching the process env.
- `None` maps every color to `Color::Reset` and keeps modifiers.
- Port Rich's 16-color palette and its `Palette.match` distance formula verbatim, as a const table.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ColorDepth::detect` unit tests: `COLORTERM=truecolor`, `COLORTERM=24bit`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM=xterm-kitty`, `TERM=rxvt-16color`, `TERM=xterm`, `TERM=dumb`, `TEXTUAL_COLOR_SYSTEM=256` override.
- [ ] `NO_COLOR` unit tests: `#0178D4` becomes `Rgb(101, 101, 101)` in truecolor, the 8-bit index of that gray in `EightBit`, and an ANSI theme gives `Reset`.
- [ ] `downsample` golden test. The script from #98 gains a mode that writes `crates/lazy-github-tui/tests/fixtures/themes/downgrade.json`: for every opaque RGB variable of all 21 themes, Rich's `Color.from_rgb(...).downgrade(EIGHT_BIT).number` and `.downgrade(STANDARD).number`. The Rust test asserts identical indices for every entry.
- [ ] `insta` snapshot: the #98 themed test widget under `textual-dark` at `EightBit` and `Standard`, showing indexed colors.
- [ ] No parity scenario (the harness pins truecolor).

## Fixtures

`crates/lazy-github-tui/tests/fixtures/themes/downgrade.json`, generated. No `parity/fixtures`.

body.title: Vendor Textual's theme palettes and resolve theme colors
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M1 App shell (#83). Sub-issue 1 of 2 of #77, which holds the shared design (types, compositing rules, fixed colors). Read #77 first.

Depends on: #62 (crate skeleton), #64 (`appearance.theme` string).

## Python reference

See #77. The values come from Textual 8.2.5 (`uv.lock`): [`theme.py` `BUILTIN_THEMES`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/theme.py#L70), [`design.py` `ColorSystem.generate`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/design.py#L106), [`color.py`](https://github.com/Textualize/textual/blob/v8.2.5/src/textual/color.py) (`blend`, `__add__`, `get_contrast_text`, `brightness`). The fallback is [`AppearanceSettings.validate_theme`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/config.py#L40-L43).

## Behavior

No new screen. After this issue, any component can ask the active theme for the exact RGB Textual would paint, for all 21 built-in theme names, with unknown names rendering as `textual-dark`.

## Out of scope

- Color depth detection and 256/16-color reduction: #99. Here `Theme::color` returns `Color::Rgb` (or a named ANSI color for the ANSI themes); #99 inserts the downsampling step.
- Using the theme in the layout, footer, table, toasts, log and status bar: #74, #76, #78, #79, #80, #81.

## Design notes

As in #77 ("Vendored, generated palettes", "Color values", "Compositing", "Fixed colors"). Specifics for this issue:

- **Generator.** `crates/lazy-github-tui/src/theme/gen/dump_themes.py` prints `palette.rs` to stdout and writes `crates/lazy-github-tui/tests/fixtures/themes/composites.json` (below). Parse values like this:
  - Text-style variables (name contains `text-style` or `link-style`) → `TextStyle`.
  - A trailing ` N%` is split off first. The base is parsed with `textual.color.Color.parse`, then the alpha is multiplied by N/100, which is what Textual's CSS parser does. `Color.parse` rejects `"ansi_blue 50%"`, hence the split.
  - `color.ansi is not None` → `Ansi`, `color.auto` → `Auto`, `transparent` and `initial` → `Transparent`, else `Rgba` (alpha = `round(a * 255)`).
  - It fails loudly on anything else, so a Textual bump can't silently drop a value.
- The generated file starts with a `// @generated by … from textual==8.2.5` header. It's excluded from `rustfmt` via `#[rustfmt::skip]` on the module, so regeneration stays diff-friendly.
- **`AnsiColor`** has the 16 named colors plus `Default`, and maps to ratatui `Color::{Black, Red, …, White}` and `Color::Reset`. Textual's `ansi_white` is ANSI 7 (ratatui `Gray`), `ansi_bright_white` is ANSI 15 (ratatui `White`), `ansi_black` is 0 and `ansi_bright_black` is 8 (`DarkGray`). Get these mappings right, because ratatui's names are offset from ANSI's.
- **`Theme::display_name`** reproduces Python's `str.title()` (an uppercase letter after every non-letter) and then `-` → space.
- **Fixed colors** (`Accent`, `RichAnsi`) live in `accent.rs` with the RGB values from #77.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `palette.rs` is generated by the committed script from Textual 8.2.5 and checked in. A test asserts `Theme::all()` yields the 21 names in Textual's order.
- [ ] `Theme::by_name` finds every built-in name and rejects `"Nord"`, `""` and `"no-such-theme"`. `Theme::from_config` returns `textual-dark` for those.
- [ ] Spot-check unit tests against Textual's output: `textual-dark` `primary_lighten_3 = #6DB2FF`, `success = #4EBF71`, `secondary = #004578`, `panel = #242F38`, `background = #121212`; `nord` `block_cursor_text_style = none`; `ansi-dark` `primary = Ansi(Blue)` and `surface = Transparent`.
- [ ] Composite parity test. The generator also writes `composites.json`: for every theme, Textual's own result (`Color.parse(bg) + Color.parse(fg)`, as `#RRGGBB`) for these pairs. A Rust test recomputes each with `ThemeColor::over` and asserts equality for all 21 themes:
  - `$text` over `$background`, `$surface`, `$panel`, `$panel-lighten-1`
  - `$text-muted` over `$surface`
  - `$foreground-muted` over `$surface`
  - `$block-cursor-foreground` over `$block-cursor-background`
  - `$block-cursor-blurred-background` over `$surface`
  - `$boost` over `$background`
  - `$foreground 5%` over `$surface` (the focused DataTable/Log tint)

  Pairs that involve an ANSI color are emitted as the ANSI name, and the test checks the `Ansi` passthrough.
- [ ] `display_name` unit tests: `textual-dark` → "Textual Dark", `catppuccin-mocha` → "Catppuccin Mocha", `rose-pine-moon` → "Rose Pine Moon", `ansi-light` → "Ansi Light".
- [ ] `Accent` and `RichAnsi` values unit-tested: `GreenYellow = #ADFF2F`, `Orchid = #DA70D6`, `RichAnsi::Green` = `#98E024` under a dark theme and `#448C27` under a light one.
- [ ] The `insta` snapshot from #77 (themed test widget under `textual-dark`, `nord`, `textual-light`, `ansi-dark`, with cell colors) is added here.

## Fixtures

- `crates/lazy-github-tui/tests/fixtures/themes/composites.json`, generated by the script. No `parity/fixtures`.

body.title: Load and save config.json compatibly with the Python app
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #64

**Stacked on #86** (Cargo workspace). The base is `rust/62-cargo-workspace`; this PR will be retargeted to `rust-main` once #86 merges.

## What changed

New module `lazy_github_core::config` (`crates/lazy-github-core/src/config.rs`, helpers in `config/lax.rs`):

- `Config` plus `AppearanceSettings`, `NotificationSettings`, `BindingsSettings`, `RepositorySettings`, `PullRequestSettings`, `IssueSettings`, `CacheSettings`, `CoreConfig`, `ApiConfig`, and the enums `IssueStateFilter`, `IssueOwnerFilter`, `MergeMethod`. Every field, default and serialization order matches `lazy_github/lib/config.py`.
- `ConfigPaths::discover()` returns `$HOME/.config/lazy-github` via `etcetera::home_dir()`. It ignores `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and doesn't use `~/Library/Application Support`. On Windows it uses etcetera's native config dir plus `lazy-github` (checked with `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`). There is also `ConfigPaths::in_dir()`, and `for_home()` for an injected home.
- `Config::default_in`, `load`, `save` and `to_json_pretty`. The output matches pydantic's `model_dump_json(indent=4)` byte for byte. Saves are atomic: the file is written to `config.json.tmp`, fsynced, then renamed into place.
- Unknown keys at the top level and inside every section go into `#[serde(flatten)] extra` maps, which keep their order through serde_json's `preserve_order`. They are written back after the known keys. That includes `api.client_type`.
- Values are coerced the way pydantic's lax mode does it, matching the behavior I checked against pydantic with `uv run`:
  - Bools accept JSON bools, `0`/`1` (and `0.0`/`1.0`), and `true/false/yes/no/on/off/t/f/y/n/1/0` in any case.
  - Ints accept integers, whole floats, bools, and trimmed strings holding an integer or a whole float.
- `auth_last_checked` is an `Option<jiff::civil::DateTime>` in pydantic's naive format, truncated to microseconds. An RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset is converted to local time. The string `"None"` loads as null; the Python settings modal writes it (bug B2, see #71).
- `bindings.overrides` is an `IndexMap<String, String>`. The strings are stored untouched, Textual key names such as `question_mark`, `slash` and `dollar_sign` included.
- Errors come back as `ConfigError`. A syntax error gives the line and column. An invalid value gives the dotted field path from `serde_path_to_error`. Both messages name the file and suggest `lazy-github clear-config`.
- `docs/rust-rewrite/PARITY.md`: the Config rows link #64. Their status is unchanged.

### Decisions worth a look

- **The default `api` section carries `"client_type": "RAW_HTTP"` in `extra`.** The acceptance criterion requires `Config::default_in(...)` to match Python's default output byte for byte, and Python always writes `client_type`. The Rust code never reads the value. A file whose `api` section lacks the key stays without it.
- `cache_directory` and `logfile_path` are `PathBuf`. They are empty only in the section structs' `Default`, and `load`/`default_in` fill them in. An explicit `""` loads as `.`, which is what Python's `Path("")` gives, so it can't be mistaken for "missing".
- Negative ints are rejected because durations are `u64`. Pydantic would accept them.

## Dependencies

- `serde_path_to_error` 0.1: dotted field paths in load errors. The spec calls for it.
- `indexmap` 2 (`serde` feature): the ordered, typed `bindings.overrides` map. The spec allows it, and `serde_json`'s `preserve_order` already pulls it in, so the build tree gains no new crate.
- `serde_json` gains the `preserve_order` feature at the workspace level, as the spec asks.
- The crate now uses `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `etcetera`, `jiff` and dev-dep `rstest`, all already declared in `[workspace.dependencies]`. I added no `tempfile`; the tests use a small temp-dir helper.

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` pass on 1.97.0.
- `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/config.rs` has 60 tests. They cover:
  - the golden fixtures: default byte-equal, full byte-equal after load and save, partial, unknown fields, lax values
  - a missing file and `{}`
  - errors: syntax line and column, trailing content, `issues.state_filter`, null list, section and path, non-string override, bad datetime, bad bools and ints
  - `auth_last_checked` round trips, offset timestamps and `"None"`
  - the Python settings-modal output (numbers saved as strings)
  - atomic save, no trailing newline, non-ASCII left unescaped
  - rstest ports of `tests/test_config.py`
  - `discover()` in a subprocess with `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set
- Fixtures are in `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/config/`. `generate.py` writes `python-default.json` and `python-full.json` from the Python app, and checks that Python loads the hand-written ones. I ran it with `HOME=/home/lazy`.
- There is no parity scenario or snapshot because this issue has no UI.

body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #88

**Stacked on #86** (the Cargo workspace, #62). The base is `rust/62-cargo-workspace`; I'll retarget it to `rust-main` once #86 merges.

## What changed

New module `lazy_github_core::gh` (`crates/lazy-github-core/src/gh/`). `lib.rs` gets one line, `pub mod gh;`, so it should merge cleanly with the parallel #64 config PR.

- `request.rs`: `Method`, `Accept` (Json / Diff / Raw / Custom) and `GhRequest`, plus a pure `argv(hostname, paginate)` that produces `api [-i] -X M [--hostname h] [--cache Ns] [--paginate] -H "Accept: …" [-H …]… [--input -] path?query`. The query string is form-urlencoded into the path in insertion order. `--cache` is added only for GET with a nonzero TTL.
- `response.rs`: `GhResponse` (`header` is case-insensitive and trims the value, plus `json`, `text` and `has_next_page`). The `-i` parser takes the status line from any `HTTP/<ver>`, accepts LF or CRLF line endings, and splits at the first blank line, so the body stays verbatim. `interpret(exit, stdout, stderr, paginated)` is the pure mapping to `GhResponse` / `GhError`. Exit 4 gives `NotAuthenticated`. A status of 300 or more gives `Http`, whose message comes from the JSON `message` field, then from stderr with `gh: ` and ` (HTTP n)` stripped, then from the reason phrase. When there's no response, `(HTTP n)` on stderr gives `Http`; otherwise it's `Command`. Exit 0 with no status line gives `Parse`. For paginated output, the stream of concatenated arrays is decoded with `Deserializer::into_iter` and flattened.
- `error.rs`: `GhError`, with the variants and messages from the spec, and `is_unauthorized`. `NotAuthenticated` suggests `gh auth login --hostname <h>` when a hostname is set.
- `cli.rs`: `GhCli` (`Arc` inner, `Default` = `"gh"` with no host) with `request`, `paginate` and `auth_status`. It spawns through `tokio::process` with stdout and stderr piped. Stdin is piped only when there's a body, and null otherwise. It sets `kill_on_drop(true)`, `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`. The body is written to stdin while the output is read (`tokio::join!`), so a large response can't deadlock. A `BrokenPipe` on that write is ignored, because the exit status explains it. Spawn `NotFound` gives `NotInstalled`. Logging uses the same `debug!` text as Python, and request bodies are never logged.

## Dependencies

- `form_urlencoded = "1"` (new workspace dependency): the spec calls for it, to encode query strings. It's small, and it's the `url` crate's own encoder.
- `lazy-github-core` now uses these existing workspace dependencies: `serde`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, and `tokio` with `io-util`, `macros` (for `join!`) and `process`. `rt` is added for tests only.

## How tested

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --locked` all pass on toolchain 1.97.0. The crate has 26 unit tests.
- `argv` tests compare exact vectors for: a plain GET, a query (space, `/`, `+`, `:`), cache (and a zero cache being omitted), a POST with a body plus a custom header, a diff Accept, `--hostname`, and a paginated GET.
- `interpret` fixture tests over `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/gh/`: 200 with HTTP/2.0 and with HTTP/1.1, 204, 404, a raw README containing blank lines and `Note: x`, exit 4, a network error, paginated success and paginated 403. They also cover header case-insensitivity and a real `Link` header with `rel="next"`. A `.gitattributes` there (`-text`) keeps the CRLF header bytes intact.
- A runner test checks that `GhCli::new("/nonexistent/gh", None)` returns `NotInstalled` for `request`, `paginate` and `auth_status`.
- A `Display` test covers every variant: one line, exact text.

## Notes for review

- **The fixtures are hand-written, not captured.** The `gh` in this environment isn't authenticated, so I couldn't record real output. I modelled them on real `gh api -i` output: the status line ends in LF, headers end in CRLF, and the request ID is scrubbed as `SCRUBBED`. Re-capturing them from an authenticated `gh` (for example `gh api -i 'repos/cli/cli/labels?per_page=1'`) would be worth doing.
- Process-level tests against `fake-gh` (stdin body delivery, `--paginate`) are deferred to whichever of this PR and #67 merges second, as the spec says.
- There's no parity scenario or snapshot, because there's no UI.

---

body.title: Parity harness: text diff and HTML report
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations. Sub-issue of #69 (parity harness), tracked in #82. See `docs/rust-rewrite/PLAN.md` §6.3.

Depends on: #92 (grid dumps and `summary.json`). It reads #93's `check.json` and `structure.json` when they exist, and works without them. Blocks: #70 (the CI artifact and job summary).

The shared spec (report layout, result rules) is in #69.

## Python reference

None. This is reporting over the dumps. The screens it shows come from the Python app as captured by #92.

## Behavior

At the end of every `cargo xtask parity` run, the harness writes these files into the report dir (#69 "Report layout"):

1. **`<scenario>/<size>/<capture>.diff.txt`**: a unified diff (3 lines of context) of `python/<capture>.txt` (`--- python`) against `rust/<capture>.txt` (`+++ rust`). It's written only when both apps captured, and is informational, never a gate.
2. **`<scenario>/report.html`**: one self-contained page per scenario.
   - **Header:** the scenario name, description, `gate`, `parity_rows`, the result badge (`pass`, `fail`, `rust-not-ready`, `python-only`, `rust-only`) and per-app status per size, from `status.json`: duration, flaky, timeout step, exit code, and fixture misses listed as keys.
   - **Per size and capture:**
     - Two panels side by side, Python on the left and Rust on the right. Each renders the grid as a `<pre>` of `<span>`s from the `runs` in `grid.json`: fg, bg, bold, italic, underline, with inverse applied by swapping. Default colors are fg `#d4d4d4` and bg `#1e1e1e`. Panels show at natural size (1 ch per cell) and scroll horizontally inside themselves on narrow viewports.
     - When an app has no capture, its panel shows the `failure.grid.json` screen if there is one, with the failure reason above it.
     - A **Highlight differences** toggle outlines every cell whose character differs between the two grids.
     - The **Structural mismatches** table from `check.json` (check, box, Python value, Rust value, message), or "not checked" when `check.json` is absent.
     - Collapsible sections: the text diff, both `structure.json` files pretty-printed, and the tail (last 50 lines) of each app's `fake-gh.log`.
   - No external assets, fonts, CDNs or frameworks. Inline CSS, plus under 100 lines of inline JS for the toggles and collapsing. Every text value from grids, logs and scenario files is HTML-escaped.
   - Box-drawing characters need a monospace stack that covers them: `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, "DejaVu Sans Mono", Consolas, monospace` with `line-height: 1.2`.
3. **`index.html`**: a table of every scenario × size, with result badges, mismatch counts and links to each `report.html`. Failed gated scenarios sort first, then `rust-not-ready`, then pass. The run's metadata goes at the top: git SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`), timestamp, OS and the flags used.
4. **`summary.md`**: Markdown for the GitHub job summary (#70). It's a heading `Parity: <n> pass, <n> fail, <n> rust-not-ready`, then a table `| Scenario | Gate | 160x48 | 100x30 | Mismatches |` using the words `pass`, `fail`, `rust-not-ready` and `skipped` (no emoji). Under it, a `<details>` list of the first 20 mismatches as `scenario/size/capture: check box: python=… rust=…`, with values cut to 80 chars. It stays under 64 KiB, which is well below GitHub's 1 MiB job-summary limit.

Sizes: a 160x48 grid with run-length styles should render to under 300 KB of HTML per capture panel. Merge adjacent runs with identical styles before emitting spans.

## Out of scope

- Producing grids and statuses: #92. Structure and checks: #93.
- Uploading the artifact and writing to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`: #70. This issue only writes `summary.md`.
- Image (PNG/SVG) screenshots: not needed, since the HTML grid is the screenshot.

## Design notes

- `xtask/src/parity/diff.rs`: `pub fn text_diff(py: &str, rs: &str) -> String`, using `similar::TextDiff::from_lines(..).unified_diff().context_radius(3).header("python", "rust")`.
- `xtask/src/parity/report.rs`: `pub fn write_reports(out: &Path, summary: &Summary) -> Result<()>`. HTML is built with plain `write!` into a `String` through a small `escape` helper. No template engine dependency, since the markup is small and fixed.
- The cell-difference highlighting is computed in Rust at report time and emitted as a CSS class on differing cells. The JS toggle only flips a class on the container, so the page works with JS disabled, just without the toggle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo xtask parity startup --python-only` writes `index.html`, `startup/report.html` and `summary.md`. The report shows the Python screen at both sizes, and the Rust panel reads "not run (--python-only)". Attach a screenshot of `report.html` to the PR.
- [ ] `insta` snapshot tests:
  - `summary.md` for a synthetic summary with one pass, one gated fail with 2 mismatches and one rust-not-ready
  - `text_diff` for two small grids
  - the HTML for a 4×2 synthetic grid pair with one differing cell, covering escaping of `<`, `&` and `"` in cell text and the diff class on the differing cell
- [ ] A test asserts the generated HTML contains no `http://` or `https://` references other than text content from the dumps, i.e. no external assets.
- [ ] The report opens correctly from a downloaded CI artifact (a local `file://`), checked by hand once and noted in the PR.
- [ ] `parity/README.md` has a "Reading the report" section.

## Fixtures

None.

body.title: Parity harness: structure extraction and structural check
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations. Sub-issue of #69 (parity harness), tracked in #82. See `docs/rust-rewrite/PLAN.md` §6.3.

Depends on: #92 (the runner and the `Grid` dump type). Blocks: #70.

The shared spec (scenario format, report layout, result rules) is in #69.

## Python reference

What the extractor has to recognize on a Python screen:

- **Pane boxes.** `LazyGithubContainer` uses `border: solid $primary-lighten-3`, and `:focus-within` changes it to `border: solid $success`. Containers collapse to `height: 3` with an `(empty)` title suffix when they have no rows ([common.py#L253-L285](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L253-L285)). Textual `solid` draws light box-drawing characters, with the border title on the top edge.
- **Titles.** `\[{key}] Repositories` ([repositories.py#L55](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/repositories.py#L55)), `Pull Requests` ([pull_requests.py#L109-L110](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/pull_requests.py#L109-L110)), `Workflows` ([workflows.py#L107-L108](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/workflows.py#L107-L108)), `Command Log` ([command_log.py#L43](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/command_log.py#L43)), and the details titles that change with the selection ([primary.py#L319-L363](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L319-L363)).
- **Status summary.** An untitled box, `border: solid $secondary`, 3 rows high ([primary.py#L100-L127](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L100-L127)).
- **Tabs.** A `TabbedContent` in the details pane ([primary.py#L136-L146](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/primary.py#L136-L146)). Textual draws a label row with an underline bar below it; the bar's segment under the active tab is highlighted.
- **Tables.** Vim-like `DataTable`s ([common.py#L33-L50](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L33-L50)): a header row in a header style, then data rows, with the cursor row highlighted.
- **Footer.** Textual `Footer` without the palette entry ([common.py#L28-L30](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/common.py#L28-L30)), on the last row. Each binding shows its key (styled) followed by its description, e.g. `q Quit`, `^p Command Pallete`.

**Rules here are v1, written from the Python source.** The implementer must check each rule against real Python dumps from #92 at 160x48 and 100x30 before writing tests. Where Textual's actual output differs, for example in which underline characters it uses, adjust the rule and record the change in `parity/README.md`. The rules double as the **rendering contract** for the Rust UI: M1 shell specs must render panes, tabs, tables and the footer so these rules recognize them.

## Behavior

### Extraction: `Grid` → `structure.json`

Run per app per capture and written to `<capture>.structure.json`:

```json
{"version":1,"size":[160,48],
 "boxes":[{"id":0,"parent":null,"title":"[1] Repositories","subtitle":"","rect":[0,3,64,40],"border_fg":"#4ebf71","focused":true,
           "tabs":null,
           "tables":[{"headers":["★","Owner","Name","Description","Private"],"rows":[["☆","parity-bot","alpha","First repo","✘"]],"cursor":0}],
           "text":["…"]}],
 "footer":[{"key":"q","label":"Quit"},{"key":"^p","label":"Command Pallete"}],
 "focused":["[1] Repositories"],
 "loose_text":["…"]}
```

The example values are illustrative; real ones come from the dumps.

1. **Boxes.**
   - **Families.** Each family is a set of corners, a horizontal char and a vertical char:

     | Family | Corners (┌ ┐ └ ┘ order) | Horizontal | Vertical |
     | --- | --- | --- | --- |
     | light | `┌┐└┘` | `─` | `│` |
     | rounded | `╭╮╰╯` | `─` | `│` |
     | heavy | `┏┓┗┛` | `━` | `┃` |
     | double | `╔╗╚╝` | `═` | `║` |
     | ascii | `+` | `-` | `|` |

     ascii only counts with all four corners present and both sides made entirely of `|`, at least 3×3.
   - **Tracing.**
     - For every top-left corner cell, scan right along the row. Accept horizontal chars and any non-border text (a title) until the first top-right corner of the same family **whose fg equals the top-left's fg**.
     - From both top corners, scan down through the family's vertical char (same fg) to the bottom corners.
     - The bottom edge must be horizontal chars or text (a subtitle).
     - The rect is `[col, row, width, height]` of the outer border.
     - Mixed-family corners, as when Textual joins adjacent borders, are accepted when the fg matches.
   - **Title** is the top edge between the corners with leading and trailing border chars and spaces stripped. Inner border-char runs, as in `─ A ─── B ─`, split the title into segments; `title` is the first segment and any others are appended with `" | "`. **Subtitle** is the bottom edge, extracted the same way.
   - **Nesting:** a box fully inside another has `parent` set to the smallest box containing it. Box order is pre-order by (row, col).
   - **Limit:** Textual `thick`, `tall`, `wide` and `blank` borders, drawn with half-blocks or spaces, are not boxes in v1. Most Python modals use `thick`. Their content still shows up in `loose_text` and in `contains` expectations. The first modal spec in M3 extends the extractor.
2. **Focus.**
   - The focus color is looked up per app in `parity/themes.toml`, keyed by the config's `appearance.theme` (default `textual-dark`), e.g. `[textual-dark] focus = "#xxxxxx"`. The value is measured from a Python dump, as the `$success` border color.
   - A box is `focused` when `border_fg` equals the focus color. The top-level `focused` field lists the titles of focused boxes in pre-order.
   - **Limits:** a theme where the focus color is also used by an unfocused border gives false positives, and a theme missing from `themes.toml` gives `focused = []` and a warning. M0 ships only `textual-dark`.
   - **Contract for Rust:** the focused pane's border uses the theme's success color and no unfocused border does.
3. **Tabs**, inside a box interior (or the full screen when not in a box):
   - **Bar row.** A row is a tab bar when its non-space cells are all in `━╸╺─▔▁`, they span at least 50% of the interior width, and they carry at least two distinct fg colors.
   - **Label row.** The row directly above the bar must contain text. Tab names are its text segments separated by 2 or more spaces, trimmed.
   - **Active tab.** The underline cells that differ in fg from the bar's most common fg form the active segment. The active tab is the name whose columns overlap it most.
   - The box gets `"tabs": {"names": [...], "active": "..."}`. The label and bar rows are excluded from `text` and from table detection.
   - **Limit:** a tab label containing two consecutive spaces is split in two.
4. **Tables**, inside a box interior after removing tab rows and nested boxes:
   - **Header row.** The first non-empty row where every text cell is bold, or has a bg different from the most common interior bg, while the row below doesn't share that style.
   - **Columns** start at the header's text segments (separated by ≥ 2 spaces), and `headers` is those segments. Each following row, until an empty row, a new header-style row or the box's bottom, is split at the column start positions and each cell is trimmed. That gives `rows`.
   - **Scrollbars.** Trailing cells from `▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█▉▊▋▌▍▎▏▐▔▕` at the right edge of the interior are removed first. So is a rightmost interior column whose bg differs from the row bg on at least half the rows.
   - **Cursor.** `cursor` is the index of the single row whose bg differs from the other rows' common bg, or `null`.
   - A box can hold several tables, e.g. stacked in the details pane.
   - **Limits:** a header cell with internal double spaces is split, and a table with no styled header isn't detected (its rows land in `text`).
5. **Footer.**
   - The last screen row, if no box covers it. Split it into style runs. The style of the first non-space run is the key style.
   - Each run in the key style starts a binding: its trimmed text is `key`, and the trimmed text of the following runs up to the next key-style run is `label`.
   - An empty last row gives `footer = []`.
   - **Contract for Rust:** footer keys are drawn in a style distinct from labels, and in Textual's key notation (`^p`, `q`, `?`). The exact notation belongs to the M1 footer spec; this check just compares strings.
6. **Text.**
   - `text` is each box's remaining interior rows, trimmed and with empty rows dropped. It ignores nested boxes, tab rows and table rows.
   - `loose_text` is the rows, or parts of rows, outside every box and the footer.
   - Both are used by `contains`/`not_contains` and shown in the report, but are **not** compared across apps: Markdown and wrapping legitimately differ.

### Checks

Two kinds per capture, both written to `<capture>.check.json` as `{"capture", "size", "expect": [<mismatch>], "cross": [<mismatch>]}`, where a mismatch is `{"check", "box", "python", "rust", "message"}`.

- **`[expect.<capture>]`**, checked against each app on its own: `pane_titles` (the ordered list of all box titles in pre-order, untitled boxes as `""`), `focused`, `tabs` (the box matched by title substring), `footer` (`"<key> <label>"` strings, in order), `contains` and `not_contains` (searched in every row of the plain text). A failure counts against that app. A Python `expect` failure always fails the run, because it means the scenario or fixtures are wrong.
- **Cross-app**, Python vs Rust, when both ran ok. Only the capture's `checks` are compared; the default is all of these:
  - `titles`: the ordered title lists are equal.
  - `tabs`: for each box title found in both, names and active tab are equal.
  - `headers`: per box title, the list of tables' `headers` is equal.
  - `rows`: per box title, `rows` are equal cell by cell, after normalization. Cells are trimmed. When one cell ends in `…` and the other starts with that cell's text minus the `…`, they're equal, because truncation width is layout, not content. The row count must match.
  - `cursor`: per box title, the `cursor` index is equal.
  - `footer`: the `(key, label)` lists are equal.
  - `focus`: the `focused` lists are equal.

  Boxes matched by `ignore.boxes` (title substring) are skipped for every check except `titles`. A box present in only one app is reported once under `titles`, not again for every other check.
- Results feed `summary.json`. Each capture gets `"check": "pass" | "fail" | "n/a"` and `"mismatches": n`, and the scenario result follows the rules in #69.

## Out of scope

- Rendering mismatches in HTML: #94. This issue only writes JSON and adds a one-line-per-mismatch section to the console output.
- Block-style (`thick`) modal borders, toasts as structure, and color comparison beyond focus: later, in the first spec that needs them (M3 modals, M1 toasts).
- Running in CI: #70.

## Design notes

- `xtask/src/parity/structure.rs`: `pub fn extract(grid: &Grid, theme: &ThemeColors) -> Structure`. It's pure, with no I/O, and is built from small passes (`find_boxes`, `assign_parents`, `find_tabs`, `find_tables`, `find_footer`, `collect_text`) that each take the grid plus a mask of cells already claimed by earlier passes.
- `xtask/src/parity/check.rs`: `pub fn check_expect(s: &Structure, e: &Expect) -> Vec<Mismatch>` and `pub fn compare(py: &Structure, rs: &Structure, checks: &[Check], ignore: &Ignore) -> Vec<Mismatch>`.
- Test grids are built from compact text fixtures under `xtask/tests/grids/*.txt`: the chars, plus an optional style layer with one letter per cell mapped to a style table. This keeps synthetic tests readable. Real Python dumps from #92 go in `xtask/tests/grids/python/` as golden inputs.
- `insta` (JSON snapshots) covers `extract` on the golden Python dumps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `extract` unit tests on synthetic grids:
  - light, rounded, heavy, double and ascii boxes
  - nested boxes
  - a title split by border runs
  - a box with a different-colored corner, which is rejected
  - a tab bar with the active segment, and a 2-space-separated label row
  - a table with a bold header, a highlighted cursor row and a trailing scrollbar column
  - a footer with alternating styles
  - an empty footer row
- [ ] Golden `insta` snapshots of `extract` on the Python `startup` dumps at 160x48 and 100x30 (from #92). The snapshot shows the expected titles (status summary `""`, `[1] Repositories` focused, the `(empty)` panes, details with its tabs) and the Repositories table headers and 3 rows. Any deviation from what the Python screen visibly shows is fixed in the rules, not accepted in the snapshot.
- [ ] `parity/themes.toml` has `textual-dark` with the focus color measured from a Python dump.
- [ ] `compare` unit tests: each check detects a single change (a title text, the title order, a tab name, the active tab, a header, a cell, the cursor index, a footer label, the focus); the `…` truncation rule; `ignore.boxes`; a box present in only one app is reported once.
- [ ] `parity/scenarios/startup.toml` gains `[expect.main]` with `pane_titles`, `focused` and `footer` taken from the Python capture. `cargo xtask parity startup --python-only` passes.
- [ ] The deliberate-change test from #69 works: a temp copy of `startup.toml` with `config_overrides.bindings.overrides = {"main.repos.focus" = "9"}` fails `expect` with a `titles` mismatch naming `[9] Repositories` and exits 1. This is an integration test in `xtask/tests/`, gated on uv being available (`#[ignore]`) and run by #70.
- [ ] `parity/README.md` documents the extraction rules, their limits and the rendering contract for the Rust UI.

## Fixtures

None new. Uses `parity/fixtures/base`.

body.title: Parity harness: scenario format, PTY runner and screen capture
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations. Sub-issue of #69 (parity harness), tracked in #82. See `docs/rust-rewrite/PLAN.md` §6.3.

Depends on: #67 (fake-gh binary and the `parity/fixtures/base` set). Blocks: #93, #94, #70.

**The shared spec is in #69.** That issue defines the CLI, the isolated environment, the scenario format (v1) and the report layout. This issue implements everything in it except the structural check (#93) and the HTML/diff output (#94).

## Python reference

See #69 → "Python reference": config under `HOME`, `first_start`, the `gh auth status` check, git detection through `LAZY_GITHUB_ORIGINAL_PWD`, and launching `.venv/bin/python -m lazy_github`. Startup flow: [app.py#L70-L103](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/app.py#L70-L103). Repos load at mount: [repositories.py#L121-L141](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/repositories.py#L121-L141).

## Behavior

- `cargo xtask parity [SCENARIO...]` with every flag listed in #69. `--retries N` re-runs a failed app run up to N times and marks it `flaky: true` if a retry passes. `--jobs N` runs scenarios in parallel (default 1). Within one scenario, sizes and apps always run one after another.
- **Scenario loading.** Parse and validate `parity/scenarios/*.toml` exactly per #69 "Scenario format (v1)". Errors carry `file:line` and exit 2. `cargo xtask parity --validate` checks every scenario file without running anything.
- **Environment.** Build `<run>` exactly as #69 "Isolated environment" says: config layering, `bin/gh` copy, git repo, cleared environment. Temp dirs are removed after the run unless `--keep-home`, which copies `home/` and `work/` into the report dir.
- **PTY runner**, per app × size:
  - Open a PTY with `portable_pty::native_pty_system()` at `PtySize { cols, rows }`. Spawn the app with `CommandBuilder`: `env_clear()`, then the allow-listed env, then `cwd = work/`.
  - A reader thread feeds the master's output into `vt100::Parser::new(rows, cols, 0)`, behind a `Mutex`, and appends the raw bytes to `pty.raw`.
  - **Query responder.** Apps block or stall on terminal queries that `vt100` doesn't answer, so the reader scans the output (keeping a tail buffer, since sequences can split across reads) and writes replies to the master:
    - `ESC[6n` (cursor position) → `ESC[<row>;<col>R`, from the parser's cursor, 1-based
    - `ESC[c` / `ESC[0c` (DA1) → `ESC[?62;22c`
    - `ESC[>c` / `ESC[>0c` (DA2) → `ESC[>0;10;1c`
    - `ESC[?<n>$p` (DECRQM) → `ESC[?<n>;0$y`
    - `ESC[?u` (kitty keyboard query) → no reply. crossterm's `supports_keyboard_enhancement` sends `ESC[?u` followed by DA1, so the DA1 reply ends its wait immediately instead of after the 2 s timeout.
  - **Steps** run in order against the shared parser:
    - `keys` are encoded with the table below and written with `key_delay_ms` pauses, and at least 100 ms after `escape` so Textual's escape-sequence timeout doesn't fuse it with the next key.
    - `type` writes the UTF-8 bytes.
    - `paste` wraps the text in `ESC[200~ … ESC[201~` when `parser.screen().bracketed_paste()` is on.
    - Waits poll every 20 ms.
    - `resize` calls `master.resize` and `parser.set_size`.
  - **Capture** first runs the implicit stability wait, then writes `<capture>.txt` and `<capture>.grid.json` (format below).
  - The whole run is bounded by `timeout_ms`. On a step timeout, a crash, or an exit before the last step, the runner writes a `failure.txt` and `failure.grid.json` dump of the current screen and records the status.
  - After the last step, it kills the child (`child.kill()`), waits up to 2 s, and drops the PTY.
- **Status and summary.**
  - Per app run, `status.json`: `{"status": "ok" | "timeout" | "exited" | "spawn-error", "step": <index or null>, "exit_code": <n or null>, "duration_ms": n, "flaky": bool, "misses": [<miss log lines from fake-gh.log>], "errors": [<fake-gh error lines>]}`.
  - A run with misses or fake-gh errors becomes `status: "ok"` with `fixture_problems: true`, and counts as a failure under #69's result rules.
  - Top-level `summary.json`: `{"version": 1, "scenarios": [{"name", "gate", "result", "sizes": [{"size": "160x48", "apps": {"python": <status>, "rust": <status>}, "captures": [{"name"}]}]}]}`. #93 adds `check` per capture. Exit code per #69.
- **Results without #93.** Until #93 lands, `result` is computed from app statuses only.

### Key encoding

| Spec | Bytes |
| --- | --- |
| printable char | its UTF-8 |
| `enter` | `\r` |
| `tab` | `\t` |
| `shift+tab` | `ESC[Z` |
| `escape`, `esc` | `ESC` |
| `backspace` | `0x7f` |
| `space` | ` ` |
| `up` `down` `right` `left` | `ESC[A` `ESC[B` `ESC[C` `ESC[D`, or `ESCOA` … when `application_cursor()` |
| `home` `end` | `ESC[H` `ESC[F`, or `ESCOH` `ESCOF` |
| `insert` `delete` `pageup` `pagedown` | `ESC[2~` `ESC[3~` `ESC[5~` `ESC[6~` |
| `f1`–`f4` | `ESCOP` `ESCOQ` `ESCOR` `ESCOS` |
| `f5`–`f12` | `ESC[15~` `ESC[17~` `ESC[18~` `ESC[19~` `ESC[20~` `ESC[21~` `ESC[23~` `ESC[24~` |
| `ctrl+a`…`ctrl+z` | `0x01`…`0x1a` |
| `alt+<c>` | `ESC` + `<c>` |

### Grid dump

`<capture>.txt` holds one line per screen row. Each line is the cell contents, with wide-char continuation cells skipped and trailing spaces trimmed.

`<capture>.grid.json` holds the full grid with run-length styles:

```json
{"version":1,"cols":160,"rows":48,"cursor":{"row":0,"col":0,"visible":false},
 "lines":[{"cells":["╭","─"," ","[","1","]"," ","R","e","p","o","…"],"runs":[{"col":0,"len":20,"fg":"#4ebf71","bg":"#1e1e1e","bold":false,"italic":false,"underline":false,"inverse":false}]}]}
```

- `cells` is the row's contents, one entry per column, with a wide-char continuation cell written as an empty string. It's stored as a JSON array of strings so column indexes stay exact.
- Colors are `"#rrggbb"` for `vt100::Color::Rgb`, `"idx:<n>"` for indexed colors and `null` for the default.
- A run covers consecutive columns with identical style.

`grid.rs` owns the `Grid` type and its (de)serialization. #93 and #94 consume it.

## Out of scope

- Structure extraction, `[expect]` checks and the cross-app comparison: #93. Until then, `checks`, `ignore` and `[expect]` are parsed and validated but not evaluated.
- `diff.txt`, `report.html`, `index.html` and `summary.md`: #94.
- CI: #70.
- The Rust UI: the Rust side reports `rust-not-ready` (scenario `gate = false`) until M1.

## Design notes

- Modules: `xtask/src/parity/{cli,scenario,env,keys,runner,grid}.rs`.
  - `scenario.rs`: serde types with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and a `Step` enum, plus custom validation for the exactly-one-key rule. Use `toml::Spanned` for line numbers.
  - `keys.rs`: `fn encode(spec: &str, app_cursor: bool) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KeyError>`.
  - `env.rs`: `fn prepare(scenario, app, size, paths) -> Result<RunEnv>`, where `RunEnv` holds the temp dirs, the `CommandBuilder` and the log path.
  - `runner.rs`: `fn run(env: RunEnv, steps: &[Step], out: &Path) -> AppRunStatus`.
- `vt100` is pinned to the version in `[workspace.dependencies]`. Screen reads always go through `parser.lock().screen()`. Nothing in the runner sleeps longer than 20 ms between checks.
- Paths: the repo root comes from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/..`. The Python venv path is `.venv/bin/python` on Unix and `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` on Windows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parity/configs/default.json` (`{"core":{"first_start":false},"api":{"client_type":"GITHUB_CLI"}}`) and `parity/scenarios/startup.toml` are committed. The scenario has `gate = false`, `sizes = [[160,48],[100,30]]`, `fixtures = ["base"]` and no git remote. Its steps wait for `Repositories`, then `capture = "main"`.
- [ ] `cargo xtask parity startup --python-only` passes on Linux and macOS. It writes `main.txt` and `main.grid.json` for both sizes, `main.txt` shows the Repositories pane listing the 3 `base` fixture repos, and `fake-gh.log` shows `auth status` plus the `/user/repos` request with no misses. Attach `main.txt` (160x48) to the PR.
- [ ] `cargo xtask parity startup` (both apps) exits 0 with the Rust side reported as `rust-not-ready`. The M0 binary just prints its version and exits.
- [ ] Unit tests:
  - Scenario parsing: a valid file; each invalid shape (two keys in one step, unknown key, `expect` naming a missing capture, a duplicate capture name, `ctrl+m`) gives an error with its line number.
  - Key encoding: every row of the table, including DECCKM on and off.
  - Config layering: overrides are deep-merged, and the forced fields win.
  - The query responder replies to a CPR request split across two reads.
- [ ] Integration test (`xtask/tests/runner.rs`, not gated on Python). Run a tiny test-only TUI binary (`xtask/tests/bin/echo_tui.rs`, built as a `[[test]]` helper or `examples/`) that draws text and echoes keys through the runner. It must cover `wait.text`, `wait.stable_ms`, `keys`, `type`, `resize` and a forced `timeout` failure with its `failure.txt`.
- [ ] A Python fixture miss, made by deleting the `/user/repos` fixture in a temp overlay, makes the run fail with exit 1 and lists the missing key in `status.json`.
- [ ] Startup median wall time for the Python app at 160x48 is noted in the PR.
- [ ] `parity/README.md`: running scenarios, the flags, the environment and the scenario format, copied from #69 and kept as the canonical doc.

## Fixtures

Uses `parity/fixtures/base` from #67. No recording needed.

body.title: Add the Github trait, User/Repository models, GhCli methods and FakeGithub
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations (#82). This is sub-issue 2 of 2 of #65, which holds the shared design. It adds the `Github` seam the TUI depends on, on top of the `gh` runner from #88.

Depends on: #88 (gh runner), #64 (`Config` for TTLs and `api.base_url`).

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/lib/github/backends/protocol.py` [`GithubApiBackend`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/protocol.py#L35-L66): generic `get`/`post`/`patch`/`put` plus `get_user`. The Rust trait is typed per endpoint instead.
- `lazy_github/lib/github/client.py` [`GithubClient.user`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/client.py#L27-L31): the current user is fetched once and memoized. `get_user` calls `GET /user` with no cache headers ([`cli.py` L177-L179](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L177-L179)).
- `lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py` [`is_logged_in_to_cli`, `assert_is_logged_in`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py#L105-L129), and [`GithubAuthenticationRequired`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py#L31-L32).
- `lazy_github/lib/github/repositories.py` [`_list_for_page` / `_list` / `list_all`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/repositories.py#L13-L54):
  - `GET /user/repos?type=all&direction=asc&sort=full_name&page=N&per_page=50`
  - cache TTL `cache.list_repos_ttl`
  - follows `Link: rel="next"` for at most 29 pages
- The caller is [`ui/widgets/repositories.py` `load_repos`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/widgets/repositories.py#L121-L131).
- `lazy_github/models/github.py`: [`User`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/models/github.py#L10-L23) (equality and hash by `id`), [`RepositoryPermission`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/models/github.py#L41-L46), [`Repository`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/models/github.py#L49-L57).

## Behavior

There's nothing on screen. What the app gets:

- `check_auth()` succeeds when `gh auth status` exits 0. It returns `GhError::NotInstalled` when `gh` is missing and `GhError::NotAuthenticated` when the user is logged out.
- `current_user()` returns the logged-in user. Only the first call runs `gh`; later calls return the memoized value, as Python does.
- `list_repositories(RepoListQuery::all())` returns every repository the user can access, sorted by `full_name` ascending. This is the same set and order as Python's `list_all()`.
  - The Python version caps the list at 29 pages × 50 repos = 1450. With `--paginate` (#88) the Rust version has no cap. It only matters to accounts with more than 1450 repos, and it is noted here as a fix rather than a parity break.
  - The list is served from `gh`'s cache for `cache.list_repos_ttl` seconds.

## Out of scope

- The low-level runner, argv, parsing and `GhError`: #88.
- Endpoints for later milestones, such as `get_repository`, the PR, issue and workflow lists, and notifications. Each feature issue adds its own methods; see "How the trait grows".
- The startup flow:
  - skipping the check while `cache.auth_last_checked` is within `cache.auth_cache_duration`
  - writing `auth_last_checked` on success
  - the "gh missing / not logged in" screen, re-checking every 5 s the way [Python's auth modal](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py#L113-L124) does

  These belong to #72.
- The unread-notification count for the status bar: #81 adds that method.

## Design notes

**Modules.** `crates/lazy-github-core/src/github.rs` holds the trait, `GhCliOptions` and the `GhCli` impl. `crates/lazy-github-core/src/models/` holds `User`, `Repository` and `RepositoryPermission`. `crates/lazy-github-core/src/github/fake.rs` holds `FakeGithub`, behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-util"))]` so the TUI crate's tests can enable it as a dev-dependency feature.

**Trait.** It uses native `async fn` in traits through return-position `impl Future + Send`, so it needs no `async_trait` dependency. Consumers are generic over `G: Github` rather than holding a `dyn Github`. The effect runner in #72 holds a `G` and clones it into spawned tasks.

```rust
pub trait Github: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn check_auth(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), GhError>> + Send;
    fn current_user(&self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<User, GhError>> + Send;
    fn list_repositories(&self, query: RepoListQuery) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<Repository>, GhError>> + Send;
}
pub struct RepoListQuery { pub kind: RepoKind /* All | Owner | Member */, pub sort: RepoSort /* FullName | Created | Updated | Pushed */, pub direction: SortDirection }
impl RepoListQuery { pub fn all() -> Self; } // All, FullName, Asc, matching Python list_all
```

**`GhCli` options.**

```rust
pub struct GhCliOptions { pub program: PathBuf, pub hostname: Option<String>, pub ttls: CacheTtls }
pub struct CacheTtls { pub default: Duration, pub list_repos: Duration, pub list_issues: Duration }
impl From<&Config> for GhCliOptions { .. }
```

- `program` defaults to `"gh"`, resolved on `PATH`. The parity harness puts `fake-gh` first on `PATH`.
- `hostname` comes from `api.base_url`. It is `None` when the host is `api.github.com` or `github.com`, so `gh` keeps its default and `GH_HOST`. Otherwise it's the URL's host, which supports GHES users. The Python CLI backend ignored `base_url`, so this only changes anything for configs that pointed the old HTTPS backend at GHES.
- `GhCli` in this issue wraps #88's runner and adds a `tokio::sync::OnceCell<User>` for the memoized current user.

**Endpoint mapping.**

| Method | Invocation | Cache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_auth` | `gh auth status [--hostname h]` | none |
| `current_user` | `gh api -i -X GET /user` | none (memoized in process) |
| `list_repositories` | `gh api --paginate -X GET "/user/repos?type=all&direction=asc&sort=full_name&per_page=50"` | `list_repos_ttl` |

`per_page=50` stays as it is in Python, so `parity/fixtures` pages can be shared by both apps.

**Models.**
- `serde` `Deserialize` and `Serialize`. Serialize is needed later by the local table caches, which must keep Python's JSON shape.
- Unknown fields are ignored. Optional fields are `Option` with `#[serde(default)]`.
- `User` equality and hashing go by `id`, as in Python.

**`FakeGithub`.** An `Arc<Mutex<..>>` of canned results per method plus a call log. `with_user(..)`, `with_repositories(..)` and `with_auth_error(GhError::..)` builders return the canned results, and `calls()` exposes the log so `update` tests in #72 can assert which requests happened.

**How the trait grows.** Every later issue that needs GitHub data does three things in its own PR:
1. Adds typed methods to `Github`, named after the action (`list_pull_requests`, `merge_pull_request`, …), with request and response models under `models/`.
2. Implements them on `GhCli` with #88's `request`/`paginate`. It uses `-i` with explicit `page`/`per_page` for lazily loaded tables and `--paginate` only where Python loops over every page. It picks the TTL from `CacheTtls`, matching the `cache_duration` the Python function passed.
3. Implements them on `FakeGithub`.

Don't add a generic `get(path)` to the trait. Keeping it typed keeps the fake small and every call site honest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `Github` trait, `GhCli` (with `From<&Config>` for its options) and `FakeGithub` (feature `test-util`) exist with the three methods above.
- [ ] `User`, `Repository` and `RepositoryPermission` deserialize from a recorded `/user` response and a recorded `/user/repos` page, and unknown fields are ignored (unit tests over JSON in `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/github/`).
- [ ] `hostname` derivation unit tests: the default `base_url` gives `None`, `https://ghe.example.com/api/v3` gives `Some("ghe.example.com")`.
- [ ] Argv for each method is asserted with a unit test, through #88's `argv`.
- [ ] `current_user` memoizes: two calls, one spawn (use a counting program path or `fake-gh`'s request log).
- [ ] `FakeGithub` unit test shows canned results and the call log.
- [ ] An integration test drives `GhCli` against `fake-gh` with `check_auth`, `current_user` and a two-page `list_repositories`. Whichever of this issue and #67 merges second adds it.
- [ ] No parity scenario or `insta` snapshot (no UI).

## Fixtures

- Unit-test JSON: one recorded `/user` response and one `/user/repos?per_page=50` page, scrubbed, under `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/github/`.
- `parity/fixtures` (for the integration test and later parity scenarios) need `gh auth status` (logged in and logged out), `GET /user`, and `GET /user/repos` with two pages linked by `Link: rel="next"`. The format belongs to #67 and recording to #68. Hand-written scrubbed fixtures are fine until #68 lands.
