body.title: Run gh api requests: argv builder, -i response parsing and GhError
body.body:
Part of the Rust rewrite, M0 Foundations (#82). This is sub-issue 1 of 2 of #65, which holds the shared design. It's the low-level `gh` process layer. The `Github` trait and the typed methods built on it come in the sibling sub-issue.

Depends on: #62.

## Python reference

- `lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py`
  - [`build_command`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L111-L134): `gh api -i -X <METHOD> -H ... -F k=v --input <tempfile> <path>`
  - [`run_gh_cli_command`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L74-L97): spawns `gh` with stdout and stderr piped, and logs `Running Github CLI command: gh ...` and `Error output from Github CLI: ...` at debug level.
  - [`_parse_cli_api_response`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L52-L66) and [`CliApiResponse`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L25-L49): success is exit code 0 and status < 300.
  - [`_create_request_body_tempfile`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L100-L108): replaced here by `--input -`.
  - [`github_headers`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/cli.py#L181-L184): sends `Cache-Control: max-age=<ttl>`. `gh` ignores that header, so the Python CLI backend effectively has no cache. Only the hishel backend honored it.
- `lazy_github/lib/github/backends/protocol.py` [`GithubApiRequestFailed`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/backends/protocol.py#L16-L20)
- `lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py` [`is_logged_in_to_cli`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/lib/github/auth.py#L105-L116): `gh auth status`, where exit code 0 means logged in.

**Known Python parser bugs. Don't reproduce them.** `_parse_cli_api_response` recognizes the status line only when it starts with `HTTP/2.0`; for `HTTP/1.1` it records status 0. It also drops every blank line in the body, and it treats any body line matching `^[a-zA-Z-]+:` as a header. JSON bodies come through intact because `gh` prints them on one line when stdout is a pipe. Raw text bodies (READMEs, diffs) get damaged. The Rust parser splits at the first blank line instead, so README and diff screens can differ from the Python app's output under the parity harness. See the note in #65.

## Behavior

There's nothing on screen. What users rely on:

- A request never writes to the terminal. `gh`'s stdout and stderr are always piped, and stdin is piped when there's a body and null otherwise.
- `gh` missing, `gh` logged out, an HTTP error and a broken response each come back as a distinct error, with a message fit to show the user (see `GhError`).
- A cancelled request kills its `gh` child: the future is dropped and the process goes with it (`kill_on_drop(true)`).

## Out of scope

- The `Github` trait, the models, `check_auth`/`current_user`/`list_repositories`, `FakeGithub`, and building `GhCli` options from `Config`: sibling sub-issue of #65.
- The startup screen that shows the auth errors: #72.
- Answering these invocations in tests: `fake-gh`, #67.
- Timeouts, retries, rate-limit handling, a concurrency cap: none exist in Python. File one if they turn out to be needed.

## Design notes

**Module.** `crates/lazy-github-core/src/gh/` (`request.rs`, `response.rs`, `error.rs`, `cli.rs`). It uses `tokio::process`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, and `form_urlencoded` for query strings.

**Request.**

```rust
pub enum Method { Get, Post, Patch, Put, Delete }
pub struct GhRequest {
    pub method: Method,
    pub path: String,                     // "/user/repos", no query
    pub query: Vec<(String, String)>,     // encoded into the path, in insertion order
    pub accept: Accept,                   // Json (default) = application/vnd.github+json, Diff, Raw, or Custom(String)
    pub headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub body: Option<serde_json::Value>,
    pub cache: Option<std::time::Duration>, // GET only; ignored otherwise
}
```

Argv, built by a pure `fn argv(&self, hostname: Option<&str>, paginate: bool) -> Vec<OsString>`:

```
api [-i] -X <METHOD> [--hostname <h>] [--cache <secs>s] [--paginate] -H "Accept: <accept>" [-H "<k>: <v>"]... [--input -] <path>[?<urlencoded query>]
```

- `-i` is on every request except paginated ones (see below).
- Query parameters go into the path rather than `-F` or `-f`. That way `gh` never applies its typed `-F` conversion or the `@file` reading, and the query looks the same for every method. (When `--input` is present, `gh` turns fields into query parameters anyway.)
- `--cache` is added only for GET with a nonzero TTL, formatted as whole seconds (`600s`).
- The body is serialized with `serde_json::to_vec` and written to the child's stdin, which is then closed.
- Process env adds `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` and `GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` and otherwise inherits, so `GH_HOST`, `GH_TOKEN` and the config dir keep working.
- Log the argv at `debug!` as `Running Github CLI command: gh <args>`, the same text as Python. Log non-empty stderr at `debug!` as `Error output from Github CLI: <stderr>`. Never log request bodies.

**Response for `-i`.** `gh -i` output is `HTTP/<ver> <code> <reason>`, then `Name: value` header lines, then an empty line, then the body bytes verbatim. Real `gh` prints the status line ending in LF and the headers ending in CRLF, so accept either line ending.

```rust
pub struct GhResponse { pub status: u16, headers: Vec<(String, String)>, pub body: Vec<u8> }
impl GhResponse {
    pub fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str>;  // case-insensitive, value trimmed
    pub fn json<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self) -> Result<T, GhError>;  // Decode on failure
    pub fn text(&self) -> String;                       // lossy UTF-8
    pub fn has_next_page(&self) -> bool;                // Link contains rel="next"
}
```

**Paginated GET.** `gh api --paginate`, with no `-i` and no `--slurp`:
- `--slurp` needs gh 2.48 or later, and combined with `-i` it emits invalid JSON.
- Output is one JSON array per page, concatenated. Parse it with `serde_json::Deserializer::from_slice(..).into_iter::<Vec<T>>()` and flatten.
- Without `-i`, the status of an error comes from the stderr suffix `(HTTP <code>)`.

Expose it as `async fn paginate<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, req: GhRequest) -> Result<Vec<T>, GhError>`. Use it only where Python fetches every page in a loop (today only `/user/repos`). Lazily loaded tables (issues, PRs, workflow runs) send explicit `page`/`per_page` query params with `-i`, as Python does. That's the PLAN §5 pagination rule, now pinned down.

**Errors.** Map the process result to an error in a pure function, `interpret(exit: Option<i32>, stdout: &[u8], stderr: &[u8], paginated: bool) -> Result<GhResponse, GhError>`, so all of it is unit-tested without spawning anything.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum GhError {
    #[error("The GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed or not on your PATH. Install it from https://cli.github.com, then run `gh auth login`.")]
    NotInstalled,                                     // spawn failed with io::ErrorKind::NotFound
    #[error("To proceed, please log into the Github CLI via `gh auth login`")]
    NotAuthenticated { hostname: Option<String>, detail: String }, // gh exit code 4, or `gh auth status` non-zero
    #[error("GitHub API request failed (HTTP {status}): {message}")]
    Http { status: u16, message: String, body: Vec<u8> },          // status >= 300 from -i, or "(HTTP n)" on stderr
    #[error("gh failed{}: {stderr}", code.map(|c| format!(" with exit code {c}")).unwrap_or_default())]
    Command { code: Option<i32>, stderr: String },    // non-zero exit and no HTTP response (network down, bad flag)
    #[error("could not parse gh output: {0}")]
    Parse(String),                                     // -i output with no status line
    #[error("unexpected response from GitHub: {0}")]
    Decode(#[from] serde_json::Error),
    #[error("failed to run gh: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
}
impl GhError { pub fn is_unauthorized(&self) -> bool; } // NotAuthenticated or Http 401
```

- `Http.message` is the body's JSON `message` field when it parses. Otherwise it's stderr with the `gh: ` prefix and the ` (HTTP n)` suffix removed.
- The `NotAuthenticated` text is the Python auth-screen sentence ([`ui/screens/auth.py`](https://github.com/gizmo385/gh-lazy/blob/main/lazy_github/ui/screens/auth.py#L38-L46)) so #72 can show it unchanged.
- When `hostname` is set, the message suggests `gh auth login --hostname <h>`.

**Runner.**

```rust
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct GhCli { inner: Arc<GhCliInner> }   // program: PathBuf (default "gh"), hostname: Option<String>
impl GhCli {
    pub fn new(program: impl Into<PathBuf>, hostname: Option<String>) -> Self;
    pub async fn request(&self, req: GhRequest) -> Result<GhResponse, GhError>;
    pub async fn paginate<T: DeserializeOwned>(&self, req: GhRequest) -> Result<Vec<T>, GhError>;
    pub async fn auth_status(&self) -> Result<(), GhError>; // `gh auth status [--hostname h]`; exit 0 = Ok, else NotAuthenticated{detail: stderr+stdout}
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GhRequest::argv` unit tests with exact argv vectors for:
  - a plain GET
  - a GET with query (encoding of spaces, `/`, `+`)
  - a GET with cache
  - a POST with body (`--input -`, no `--cache`)
  - a diff Accept
  - `--hostname`
  - a paginated GET (no `-i`)
- [ ] `interpret` unit tests over captured outputs in `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/gh/`:
  - 200 with `HTTP/1.1` and with `HTTP/2.0` status lines, CRLF headers and a JSON body
  - 204 with an empty body
  - 404 with a JSON error body and the `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` stderr, giving `Http{404, "Not Found"}`
  - a raw README body containing blank lines and a `Note: x` line, kept verbatim
  - exit 4 with empty stdout, giving `NotAuthenticated`
  - exit 1 with empty stdout and a network error on stderr, giving `Command`
  - paginated output of two concatenated arrays, flattened
  - paginated failure with `(HTTP 403)` on stderr, giving `Http{403}`
- [ ] Header lookup is case-insensitive. `has_next_page` reads a real `Link` header.
- [ ] `GhCli::new("/nonexistent/gh", None).request(..)` returns `GhError::NotInstalled`, and so does `auth_status`.
- [ ] Every `GhError` variant's `Display` is a single readable sentence (unit test over each variant).
- [ ] No parity scenario or `insta` snapshot (no UI). Process-level tests against `fake-gh` (stdin body delivery, `--paginate`) are added by whichever of this issue and #67 merges second.

## Fixtures

Unit-test fixtures only: captured `gh api -i` stdout and stderr pairs under `crates/lazy-github-core/tests/fixtures/gh/`.
- Capture them from a real `gh` (any public endpoint, e.g. `gh api -i repos/cli/cli/labels?per_page=1`).
- Scrub `Github-Authentication-Token-Expiration` and request IDs.
- Hand-write the error cases.

No `parity/fixtures` entries.

body.title: Add CI for rust-main: fmt, clippy and tests on Linux and macOS
body.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"gizmo385"} -->
_Requested by **Chris** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv9?thread=cmsg_012pc8Wphbdkgs8rn26pJBv91YRDXqF1kGmJaE3iA28mKh)_

Closes #63

**This PR is stacked on #86** (the #62 Cargo workspace), so its base is `rust/62-cargo-workspace`. Once #86 merges, I'll retarget it to `rust-main`. The diff is one file.

## What changed

New workflow `.github/workflows/rust.yaml`:

- **Triggers:** `push` and `pull_request` on `rust-main`.
- **Permissions:** `permissions: contents: read`.
- **Matrix:** `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`, with `fail-fast: false` so each OS reports its own result. Windows is left out until M5, per PLAN.md §7 and §10.
- **Steps:**
  1. `actions/checkout@v6`
  2. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` with `rustfmt, clippy`. That action has no version tags; its refs are toolchain names. Rustup applies `rust-toolchain.toml` to every cargo call, so the file stays the source of truth for the channel and components.
  3. `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`
  4. `cargo fmt --all --check`
  5. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  6. `cargo test --workspace`
- **Concurrency group:** a new push to the same ref cancels the run already in progress.
- **Not touched:** `.github/workflows/code-checks.yaml`.

## Dependencies

No new crates. The GitHub Actions used:

- `actions/checkout@v6`: checks out the repo. v7 tags exist, but I couldn't check their release notes from this session, so I stayed on v6.
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`: the action the spec names. It installs the stable toolchain, which matches `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`: the cache action the spec names. It caches `~/.cargo` and `target/` per OS and lockfile.

## How I tested it

- The workflow YAML parses. The triggers and the job are as specified.
- Locally, a deliberately misformatted `crates/fake-gh/src/main.rs` makes `cargo fmt --all --check` exit 1. Restoring the file brings it back to exit 0. I didn't commit the misformatted file.
- `git diff origin/rust-main -- .github/workflows/code-checks.yaml` is empty.
- The fmt, clippy and test commands all pass locally on Linux (see #86).

**Pending:** Two acceptance criteria can only be checked in Actions:

- the workflow runs green on a PR into `rust-main`
- the misformatted-file check fails the CI job

Because the base is `rust/62-cargo-workspace`, the `pull_request` trigger won't fire until this PR is retargeted to `rust-main`. The first real run will be after that. Once these checks run, they can also become required in `rust-main` branch protection.

I haven't enabled auto-merge. `rust-main` has no branch protection yet, so turning it on would merge the PR with no review.

body.title: Pick a text-input crate compatible with ratatui 0.30 (tui-textarea 0.7 needs ratatui 0.29)
body.body:
Found while setting up the Cargo workspace (#62).

PLAN.md §4 picks `tui-textarea` for text input. Its latest release, 0.7.0 (Oct 2024), depends on `ratatui ^0.29` and `crossterm ^0.28`, while the current releases are `ratatui` 0.30.2 and `crossterm` 0.29.0. Using it means either holding the whole workspace on ratatui 0.29, or picking a maintained alternative.

Candidates seen on crates.io:
- `ratatui-textarea` 0.9.3 (updated 2026-10-05, ~620k recent downloads)
- `tui-textarea-2` 0.13.2 (updated 2026-08-23)
- Pin `ratatui` 0.29 + `crossterm` 0.28 and keep `tui-textarea` 0.7.

The #62 workspace declares `ratatui = "0.30"` and `crossterm = "0.29"` and leaves the text-input crate out of `[workspace.dependencies]`, with a comment pointing here. Per PLAN.md §4, swapping a crate is a design decision.

Recommendation: `ratatui-textarea`, if it covers the same API (multi-line editing, single-line mode, key input handling) on ratatui 0.30. Then update PLAN.md §4 and add it to the workspace dependencies.
